articleTitle: Intensive Tasks Offloading Decision Algorithms in Satellite Edge Computing Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: To address the offloading allocation problem for intensive tasks in Satellite Edge Computing (SEC) systems, a Sequence-to-Sequence (Seq2Seq) and Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) based decision generation algorithm, enhancing resource allocation efficiency in SEC systems.

articleTitle: Cache-Assisted Task Offloading and Resource Optimization for LEO Network
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We proposed a cache-assisted task offloading and resource allocation model and a deep reinforcement learning (DRL) based method for low-earth orbit (LEO) network. Our method takes obvious advantages in reducing delay and energy consumption.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Ant Colony Optimization and Tabu Search Algorithm for Routing Optimization in LEO Satellite Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: To optimize routing costs and communication delays in LEO satellite networks, a hybrid ACO and tabu search algorithm is proposed. Simulation results shows compared to the original ACO algorithm, it reduced routing costs and delay.

articleTitle: Regional Resilient Routing Algorithm for LEO Satellite Network
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A hierarchical deep reinforcement learning-based regional resilient satellite routing algorithm is proposed. The simulation result shows the proposed method improves the communication success rate of the network in the event of regional damage.

articleTitle: A Simple and Generalizable Algorithm for Multimode Fiber Specklegram Based Deformation Sensor
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A K Nearest Neighbors based algorithm is proposed for multimode fiber specklegram based deformation sensor. This algorithm well balances the complexity and generalization of deformation detection, which is validated by experimental results.

articleTitle: A Multi-Domain Protection for Reliable Slicing in Network Coding Based 5G/B5G RAN Enabled Power Distribution Network
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: This paper first discusses a multi-domain protection for reliable slicing in network coding based 5G/B5G RAN enabled power distribution network. A network coding based CensNet enhanced Deep Reinforcement Learning algorithm (NC-CensNet-DRL) is proposed.

articleTitle: Intra-Vehicle Optical Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Intelligent connected vehicles require high bandwidth due to the increased sensors and improved architectures. Optical communications provide several advantages over copper cables in intra-vehicle networks, but face many challenges, especially the harsh operating environment.

articleTitle: Efficient Training of Large-Scale Optical Neural Network Based on Evolutionary Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this article, we introduce a novel learning mechanism based on evolutionary algorithm to train subspace optical neural networks (SONNs). To demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed covariance matrix adaptation evolution strategy (CMA-ES), the trained SONNs are applied in a typical MNIST dataset classification task. The calculated results demonstrate that the accuracy and stability of the training method are competitive with the traditional gradient algorithm, but the SONNs trained by the CMA-ES can achieve 1.5 times acceleration.

articleTitle: Power Optimization for S+C+L-Band Transmission Using a Self-Adaptive Differential Evolution Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We propose a differential evolution algorithm-based technique, using uniform or non-uniform power optimizations, to mitigate the SRS impact on S+C+L-band transmission. The optimized GSNR flatness can be reduced from 4.61 dB to 0.45 dB.

articleTitle: Optoelectronic Pod Integrating FSO Communication and Scanning Based on Liquid Crystal Optical Phased Array
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Addressing the issues associated with traditional mechanical scanning methods, such as large size, complex and heavy structures, slow response speed, susceptibility to mechanical damage, and high maintenance costs, this paper proposes an all-solid-state beam scanning method based on a liquid crystal phased array(LCOPA). A cascaded wide-angle beam steering model is established, overcoming the limitation of traditional mechanical beam scanning that prevents high-speed jumps, achieving continuous and agile beam steering within a two-dimensional range of -24° to 24°. Additionally, a high-precision beam steering angle compensation scheme and voltage pre-driving technology are proposed, achieving a large-angle beam deflection response time of 5ms, a fine beam deflection fastest response time of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{300}\boldsymbol{\mu}\mathbf{s}$</tex>, and a beam steering accuracy of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{10}\boldsymbol{\mu}\mathbf{rad}$</tex>. The feasibility and correctness of the non-mechanical beam deflection scheme based on the LCOPA are demonstrated, showing promise for high-efficiency non-mechanical laser ATP tracking, high-speed free-space communication, and rapid target detection.

articleTitle: Key Enablers for Hardware-Efficient Neural Network Receiver in Short-Reach Optical Links
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: This paper systematically studies hardware-efficient neural network-based equalization techniques for short-reach direct-detection optical systems. Transfer learning can be utilized for accelerating the training procedure, while pruning, multi-task learning and quantization are proposed for efficient equalization.

articleTitle: All-Fiber Coaxial Focus Multimode Beam Probe for Optical Coherence Tomography
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Breaking through the limitation of depth-of-focus (DOF) and lateral resolution in fiber focusing optics for optical coherence tomography (OCT) has been challenging. In this paper, we propose an all-fiber coaxial focus multimode beam probe for high resolution OCT imaging applications. A DOF of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{820}\ \boldsymbol{\mu} \mathbf{m}$</tex> and a lateral resolution of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{4.9}\ \boldsymbol{\mu}\mathbf{m}$</tex> were achieved experimentally. It is demonstrated that the proposed OCT probe can precisely profile the layer-by-layer structure of a multi-layer translucent tape, revealing more refined details.

articleTitle: Thin-Film Lithium Niobate Modulator Formed by 3D Electrodes on Mach-Zehnder Interferometer
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We propose a thin-film lithium niobate (TFLN) modulator based on 3D electrodes with a typical design of the modulator with a modulation arm length of 5 mm to achieve a bandwidth of 151 GHz.

articleTitle: High-Gain L-Band Extended Fiber Amplifier Using Bismuth-Erbium Co-Doped Fiber
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A high-gain L-band extended fiber amplifier using bismuth-erbium co-doped fiber is investigated. The pre-amplifier and the double-pass configuration are used to improve the gain performance. The achieved 20-dB gain bandwidth is 61 nm (1557~1618 nm) with a 3-dB flatness bandwidth of 35 nm (1565~1600 nm), maximum gain of 51.95 dB, and minimum noise figure of 4.17 dB.

articleTitle: Research on Effective Separation Method of Multi-Molecule Composite Absorption Spectrum Based on Modulation Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: ‘Carbon Peak And Carbon Neutrality’ is an important goal of China's current economic development. Therefore, it is crucial to detect the greenhouse gases such as CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, and the main products in the process of carbon emissions such as H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O and CO. In this paper, two lasers with wavelengths of 1570 nm and 1985 nm are selected to realize the simulation verification of the simultaneous measurement method of H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O, CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> and CO. A multi molecule composite absorption spectroscopy separation method is proposed in this article. Based on tunable diode laser absorption spectroscopy technology, the concentration information of H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O and CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> is obtained sequentially by fitting the normalized second harmonic signal after deducting the background. Then, using this as the background, it is substituted into the composite absorption spectrum, and the spectral information of CO is obtained through sub-channel deduction, achieving effective separation of the absorption spectrum. The simulation results show that the maximum absolute deviations of the three gases are 0.21%, 1.83% and 2.72%, respectively, which provides strong support for the engineering application of wavelength modulation technology to simultaneously measure multiple components.

articleTitle: Gap Phase-Shifted Fiber Bragg Grating and Its Application
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A gap phase-shifted fiber Bragg grating (g-FBG) formed by cutting off a conventional FBG and re-coupling is proposed and demonstrated. Furthermore, a reflection g-FBG is put forward and investigated. The g- FBG can be implemented easily and used in optical spectrum filtering, tuning, and multiparameter sensing with better sensitivity and resolution.

articleTitle: Research on OAM Multiplexing System Based on Atmospheric Turbulence Channels
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Orbital angular momentum is widely applied to multiplexing communication systems. However, there are few reports on those systems based on the non-Kolmogorov turbulence. We conducted research on this topic and optimized the bit error rate.

articleTitle: Characterization of Phase Shift in UTC Photodiode and MUTC Photodiode
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The characterizations of phase shift for UTC-PD and MUTC-PD are studied with a variation of light intensity and bias voltage. Both the thinner depleted region and higher operation bias voltage can bring a higher electric field in depleted layer, thereby counteract the impact of self-induced electric field on electron velocity. Thus, we conclude that thickness of depleted region and operation bias voltage can affect the stability of PD's phase. It is also demonstrated that the extreme values of electron transit-time correspond to extreme points of phase change and AM-to-PM null points through calculation. Besides, the stability of electron velocity is proved to determine the stability of phase shift with a variation of optical power.

articleTitle: Weighted BIRCH Algorithm for Probabilistic Shaping 64QAM Coherent Optical Communication System
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The Weighted BIRCH algorithm is proposed to mitigate the fiber nonlinearity for PS-64QAM signals. Experimental results demonstrate that compared with the traditional BIRCH, the proposed algorithm improves the dynamic range of fiber-launched power by 1.4 dBm.

articleTitle: A Vector Wind Speed Sensor Based on Cylindrical Cantilever Beam Structure
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Real-time and accurate measurement of wind speed is crucial for the safe operation of power transmission networks. However, existing wind speed sensors struggle to accurately measure wind speed and direction in the high electromagnetic interference environment of transmission lines. To address this issue, a vector wind speed sensor based on fiber Bragg grating (FBG) technology is designed. Experimental results indicate that with a cylindrical rod diameter of 3mm, length of 200mm, and a sensitivity sphere diameter of 63mm, the sensor achieves a sensitivity of 7. <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$8\mu\varepsilon/(m/s)$</tex> within the wind speed range of 0–15 m/s and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$8. 3\times 10^{2}\mu\varepsilon/(m/s)$</tex> within the range of 15–30 m/s. ANSYS fluid-structure interaction simulations show that the sensor introduces Kármán vortex street oscillations in the direction perpendicular to the wind speed during measurement. To mitigate this oscillation, we propose modifying the sensitivity sphere to an ellipsoidal shape, and ANSYS simulations confirm the feasibility of this approach. The fiber Bragg grating vector wind speed sensor, based on a cylindrical cantilever beam and composite sensitivity sphere structure, has significant application prospects in the power transmission industry.

articleTitle: Prediction of tidal flat settlement based on array displacement meter and Mamba model
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, an array displacement meter based on micro electro mechanical system (MEMS) is used to monitor the settlement of a tidal flat in Dinghai District, Zhoushan, Zhejiang Province. A settlement prediction method based on structured state space sequence model Mamba is proposed. Empirical studies on multiple sensor nodes show that the proposed method is superior to previous methods and provides highly accurate predictions. The results of this study will enrich the theory and method of monitoring and forecasting the topographic settlement of tidal flats.

articleTitle: Harnessing the Potential of Advanced Large Vision Models to Enhance the Detection of Optoelectronic Imaging Signals
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: This study focuses on exploring the use of SAM (Segment Anything Model), an advanced visual foundation model, to enhance the detection of optoelectronic imaging signals. We fine-tuned the mask encoder of SAM and used the Electron Microscopy Dataset as the experimental dataset. To evaluate the effect, the U-net model was also used as a comparison benchmark. The experimental results show that the IoU metrics of SAM outperform those of U-net when only a small amount of data is available, demonstrating that the fine-tuned SAM has a unique advantage in recognizing photoelectric imaging signals.

articleTitle: Dual silicon microring resonators for carbon dioxide gas sensing
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We proposed dual microring resonators with SiO2 and polyhexamethylene biguanide hydrochloride claddings for CO2 sensing with temperature compensation, achieving a simulated sensitivity of 3.6 pm/ppm. Then we fabricated dual microrings and conducted temperature-response measurements.

articleTitle: High-Speed Optical Signal Identification Scheme Based on Multidimensional Fractal
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, a high-speed optical signal identification scheme based on multidimensional fractals. Results demonstrate that the proposed scheme achieves 100% MFI accuracy at optical signal-to-noise ratio (OSNR) ≥18 dB.

articleTitle: CNN-BiGRU Fiber Nonlinear Compensation Scheme Based on Multi-Label Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We propose a CNN-BiGRU fiber nonlinear compensation scheme based on multi-label classification, which improves Q-factor performance compared with multi-class classification and regression schemes.

articleTitle: Key Secure Technologies for Optical Satellite Network
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: For the space information network, different attacks bring serious security issues. In order to overcome these shortcomings, this paper summarizes the key secure technologies and corresponding challenges for optical satellite networks.

articleTitle: A Highly Efficient Unsupervised Recognition Method for Fiber-Optic DAS with Spiking Convolutional Neuron Network (SCNN)
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper an efficient unsupervised spiking convolutional neural network (SCNN) is proposed for the first time to improve the event recognition performance and timeliness simultaneously in the fiber-optic distributed acoustic sensor (DAS). Its effectiveness is validated through three groups of field tests, including small dataset A with balanced, typical and consistent data, bad datasets B and C full of inconstant and atypical data, and fully imbalanced dataset D respectively. It improves its computation efficiency by six times while maintaining its stably high recognition accuracy compared with the standard SNN; while compared with the mainstream supervised CNN, the SCNN has a stronger generalization ability with complicated inconsistent, or imbalanced samples, which often happens in practice.

articleTitle: DRL-based Impairment-aware Resource Allocation Algorithm in C + L Band Elastic Optical Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We propose an impairment-aware resource allocation algorithm for C+L-band elastic optical networks based on deep reinforcement learning (DRL). Simulation results show that the proposed algorithm effectively reduces the blocking probability by over 10.9%.

articleTitle: Liquid Level Measurement by Using Waist-Enlarged Fusion Taper in No-Core Fiber
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A liquid level measurement approach based on modal interferometer (MI) using no-core fiber (NCF) is proposed. A section of NCF with a length of 80 mm is fused into waist-enlarged fusion tapers (WEFTs) structure to form an MI, which can excite high-order mode to measure the liquid level change. Experimental results show a sensitivity of up to 0.093 nm/mm.

articleTitle: Forward Brillouin Sensor with High Spatial Recognition and Multiplexing Positioning Capabilities for Flow and Bubble Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A novel optical fiber sensor for flow and bubble detection based on forward Brillouin sensing (FBS) is proposed, which has the most advanced spatial recognition of FBS and for the first time sub-centimeter positioning capability.

articleTitle: Efficient On-Chip Waveguide Characterization Using Image Processing Algorithm in Optical Lithography
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We demonstrate an image processing algorithm for fast measuring waveguide chip dimensions during the optical lithography processing as an assistant tool for adjusting the fabrication parameters and improving the yield rates of the photonic chips.

articleTitle: Experimental Demonstration on Modified CAZAC Matrix-Based Precoding for OFDM/QNSC
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: This paper proposes a modified CAZAC Matrix-based precoding scheme for OFDM/QNSC system. Experimental results verify that our scheme achieves a ~1.2dB PAPR reduction and ~2dB BER improvement compared to original CAZAC matrix.

articleTitle: Research on pH Sensor Based on Micro-Nano Fiber Modified with Calcium Alginate Hydrogel
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We presented a novel pH sensor based on micro-nano fiber (MNF) modified with calcium alginate hydrogel. Two biocompatible polyelectrolytes, sodium alginate (NaAlg) and calcium chloride (CaCl<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>), were chemically reacted to form a calcium alginate hydrogel with three-dimensional network structure, which was coated on the surface of MNF for pH sensing. When the pH of surrounding solution changes, the sensor has a high sensitivity and linear correlation in the pH range of 2–9 due to the change in the refractive index of the hydrogel. The sensitivity of the single-layer and three-layer hydrogel-coated MNF sensor is -1.57 nm/pH, -2.50 nm/pH, respectively, which makes the sensor very promising for physiological sensing applications.

articleTitle: Temporal Characteristics of Nonlinear Crosstalk in the Presence of Inter-Channel Stimulated Raman Scattering
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We investigated the autocorrelation of nonlinear interference noise (NLIN) and the result shows that the temporal correlation of NLIN is significantly wavelength dependent in ultra-wideband WDM systems due to inter channel stimulated Raman scattering.

articleTitle: Viewpoint Rotation Prediction based Resource-Efficient Holographic Type Communication in EON enabled 6G RAN
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A LSTM based viewpoint rotation prediction enabled resource-efficient holographic type communication is investigated in EON enabled 6G RAN. The CensNet enhanced PPO is used for feature extraction based DU-CU deployment and RSA, with 40.1% joint objective reduction than benchmark.

articleTitle: Intent-Driven Routing Algorithm Based on LSTM in Power Backbone Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We propose a method combining Long Short-Term Memory Neural Network with Conditional Random Fields to achieve intention translation routing in power backbone networks. Simulation results show that it can improve the accuracy of the translation.

articleTitle: High-Resolution Spatial Speckle Reconstructive Spectrometer Based on Random Reflection
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: An ultra-compact reconstructive spectrometer with high-performance utilizing random reflection is proposed. Experimentally, the spectrometer has a resolution of 0.02 nm within the range of 50 nm and its footprint is 220 μm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2.</sup>

articleTitle: Gain Optimization of Lithium Niobate Ridge Waveguide Amplifiers
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: An erbium-doped lithium niobate waveguide amplifier covered with an erbium and ytterbium co-doped aluminum oxide cladding layer is designed. Combine with the light field confinement factor and the effective mode area to optimize the mode field distribution. The modal gain of the amplifier was calculated to be 30 dB by numerical simulations based on the theoretical model of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{Er}^{\mathbf{3}+}-\mathbf{Yb}^{\mathbf{3}+}$</tex> co-doped.

articleTitle: An Enhanced Polar-LDPC Concatenated Protection Scheme Utilizing Optimized Critical Sets
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Polar codes are a class of coding schemes that have been theoretically proven to achieve the capacity in binary-input memoryless symmetric channels, thereby becoming a prominent research focus in communications research. Although polar codes theoretically approach the Shannon limit as the code length increases indefinitely, their performance is inherently limited at finite-length codes due to incomplete channel polarization. To address this limitation, we propose an optimized critical sets(OCS) selection method specifically designed for error sets within polar codes, aiming to optimize the selection strategy for intermediate-quality channels. Subsequently, a polar-LDPC concatenated protection scheme is introduced, which utilizes the OCS to effectively protect the error set information bits, thus enhancing the overall protection scheme. The simulation results show that the OCS approach exhibits a more precise selection of intermediate-quality channels, resulting in a significant performance improvement of approximately 1 dB compared to alternative protection schemes.

articleTitle: Fiber Mapping Using Neural Networks for Physical-Layer Secure Key Distribution
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Neural networks are applied for fiber mapping in unidirectional physical-layer key distribution, where the bi-directional long short-term memory increases the key generation rate from 12.28 to 13.68 Gbps.

articleTitle: Strain and Temperature Discrimination Measurement Sensor Using FMF- PMF Fiber Structure Built in Sagnac Loop
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A segment of few mode fibre (FMF) is sandwiched between single mode fibre (SMF) and polarization maintaining fiber (PMF), misaligned fusion splicing of FMF and SMF, proposed FMF-PMF fiber configuration is constructed a Sagnac loop.

articleTitle: L-Band Extended EDFA Co-Pumped by C-Band Laser
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A two-stage L-band extended erbium-doped fiber amplifier (LE-EDFA) with 20 dB gain bandwidth covering 1570–1622 nm and a minimum noise figure of 5.0 dB is demonstrated by employing a high-power C-band laser as the co-pump source.

articleTitle: Mechanism and Optimal Working Conditions of Photoelectric Frequency Down-Conversion Based on Photodetectors
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, the optoelectronic frequency down-conversion characteristics of uni-traveling carrier photo detectors in the communication band of 1550 nm are investigated, and the generation mechanism of photoelectric mixing is explained based on the electron mobility model in the collection region of the device. The influence of various operating conditions of the photodetector on the down-conversion output power is analyzed, and based on this, a systematic study is carried out to select the optimal down-conversion operating conditions, which shows that the bias-radio frequency (RF) output power curves can accurately characterize the photodetector's output performance of optoelectronic frequency down-conversion, further enhancing the gain of the photoelectric mixing.

articleTitle: Directional Antenna UAVs Networking Algorithm Based on On-Demand-Weighted Clustering
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: To solve the problem of cluster configuration for unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) networks in highly dynamic environments, a directional antenna UAVs network algorithm based on demand-weighted clustering is proposed to enhance stability and adaptability.

Index Terms: Speed Of The Unmanned Aerial Vehicles

articleTitle: Spin Hall Effect of Electromagnetic Wave Based on Hyperbolic Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this work, a hyperbolic metasurface is proposed to investigate the spin Hall effect of electromagnetic wave based on the dispersion relation control and the unidirectional propagation phenomenon has been numerically realized.

articleTitle: Sensing Characteristics of Long Period Fiber Grating Written in Graded Index Fiber by CO2 Laser
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We present a long period fiber grating, which can measure temperature, curvature, refractive index, torsion, and the corresponding sensitivities are 500.71 pm/°C, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$- {16}{{.53\ nm/}}{{\mathrm{m}}^{ - 1}}$</tex>, -2776.19 nm/RIU, and -193.65 pm/(rad/m), respectively.

articleTitle: Accurate and Efficient Fiber Channel Modeling for Complex-Value Based Conditional Generative Adversarial Network
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: This paper presents a model of a standard single-mode fibre channel constructed using a complex-valued conditional generation adversarial network (CV-CGAN). The model is validated using a 120 Gb/s signal with single-polarised 16 QAM, demonstrating an NMSE improvement of 41.98%.

articleTitle: Indoor High Precision LED Visible Light Positioning Based on Binaural Effect Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: An indoor multi-dimensional light-emitting diode (LED) visible light positioning (VLP) method based on binaural effect algorithm (BEA) has been proposed with the five-dimensional position coordinate including the vertical and horizontal inclination angles of the target. Specifically, the impact of the line-of-sight (LOS) link and non-line-of-sight (NLOS) link are both considered. The fitness function that includes five-dimensional coordinate has been proposed, and BEA is designed and applied to the VLP system to search the position of the global optimal solution.

articleTitle: UTC-PD Optoelectronic Mixer Designment and Mixer Array
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We propose an optoelectronic mixing array for millimeter wave (MMW) and Terahertz (THz) system which achieves conversion loss of 8.9 dB and 10.5 dB at LO frequency of 60GHz and 100GHz.

articleTitle: A Subset Quadratic Mapping PS-TCM Scheme Based on Huffman Coding
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A subset quadratic mapping PS-TCM scheme based on Huffman coding is proposed to increase transmission capacity. Simulation results show that compared to CCDM-shaped PS-TCM-16QAM and uniform TCM-16QAM signals, Huffman-coding PS-TCM-12QAM signals can improve BER performance.

articleTitle: Hot-Wire Anemometer Using Cobalt-Doped Fiber-Based Mach-Zehnder Interferometer
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A hot-wire anemometer by using a two-arm optical fiber Mach-Zehnder interferometer (MZI) is proposed. A 5mm-long cobalt-doped fiber (CDF) is inserted in the sensing arm of the MZI and optically heated to a high temperature over the environmental by using a 1480 nm heating laser. The interference fringe of the CDF-based MZI shifts with airflow velocity due to cooling effect of the airflow. Airflow velocity is therefore measured by detecting wavelength shift of the interference fringe. In experimental measurement, high sensitivity of -2.1 nm/(m/s) is achieved at airflow velocity of 0.1 m/s and the measurement range is 0-2.0 m/s. The CDF-based MZI hot-wire anemometer possesses several advantages including high sensitivity, simple structure, easy fabrication and low cost.

articleTitle: Observations of Switchable Polarization Temporal Kerr Cavity Solitons
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Temporal cavity solitons (CSs) are self-organized localized structures that can develop, persist, and stably transmit in coherently driven nonlinear optical resonators, and thus have widespread applications ranging from optical communication to optical computing. Recent investigations have revealed that scalar (vector) CSs can be formed in single-component (or two-component) Kerr resonator systems, which exhibit unique properties and dynamics. Here, we investigate a Kerr resonator consisting of single-mode and polarization-maintaining fibers and report the experimental observations of switchable polarization CSs in a monochromatically driven resonator. Our experimental work advances the understanding of the essence and mechanism of nonlinear optical phenomena while also expanding our grasp of temporal CSs in passive Kerr resonators.

articleTitle: Fault Diagnosis for Power Backbone Networks based on Graph-Gated Knowledge Graph
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We propose a fault diagnosis method for back-bone transmission networks based on graph-gated knowledge graph. Simulation results show that it can effectively improve the fault diagnosis accuracy.

articleTitle: An Efficient and Trustworthy Sharing Scheme for Multi-Domain Optical Resources Based on Blockchain
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, we propose an efficient and trustworthy sharing scheme for multi-domain optical resources based on blockchain to ensure the security and enhance the efficiency of resource exchange across optical networks. Compared with traditional Ethereum, simulation results show that our model significantly improves the transaction processing speed (TPS).

articleTitle: Performance Assessment of Deep Learning based Channel Modeling for Fiber Optic Communication System
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We compare and study three data-driven channel modeling methods based on deep learning in fiber optic communication systems. TTHNet performing the best among three networks with lower channel fitting error and best system BER performance.

articleTitle: Two-Photon Polymerization 3D-Printing for Fabricating Tall Structures on Optical Fiber Tips
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The research provides insights into fabricating tall structures directly on optical fiber tips using two-photon polymerization 3D-printing. Various geometries were tested and the quality of the print was discussed. A structure with a height of 6 mm was successfully printed, establishing the current limit of on-fiber fabrication. The research also highlights functional tall devices fabricated with this method, such as photonic crystal fiber segments, axicons and lenses.

articleTitle: Modulation Format Recognition Scheme Based on Reinforcement Learning in Coherent Optical Communication System
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: This paper proposes a modulation format recognition scheme based on reinforcement learning. Its effectiveness is validated in a 32Gbaud 1000km transmission experiment. It can achieve recognition of five high-order modulation formats under low OSNR conditions.

articleTitle: Designing Mode Conversion Metasurface Based on Simulated Annealing and Genetic Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Metasurfaces can achieve directional control of light, optical imaging and sensing applications, polarization control, and have numerous applications in the field of optics. We propose a design method for generating mode conversion metasurfaces based on simulated annealing and genetic algorithms. In this method, simulated annealing algorithm is used to design the phase profile, and genetic algorithm optimizes the phase variation from random disturbance to intelligent generation, and the phase profile is optimized by the simulated annealing algorithm. Variation from random disturbance to intelligent generation, achieving precise mode conversion and improving computational speed. The phase profile designed by the algorithm is then used to optimize the phase profile. The phase profile designed by the algorithm is then converted into the geometry and arrangement of each unit in the metasurface structure. Mode conversion is achieved by controlling the phase of light. Moreover, the generated metasurface layout can achieve the transformation between arbitrary input and output Linear Polarization(LP) modes, enhancing the accuracy of mode overlap in lasers. Moreover, the generated metasurface can achieve the transformation between arbitrary input and output LP modes, enhancing the accuracy of mode overlap in multimode lasers.

articleTitle: Coherent pulse compression ranging based on an acousto-optic frequency shifting loop
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A laser ranging system based on an acousto-optic frequency shifting loop (AO-FSL) is demonstrated using coherence pulse compression. Linearly frequency-modulated waveforms (LFMWs) with a 10-GHz bandwidth in the range of 6 GHz ~ 16 GHz are generated by tuning the shifted frequency in AO-FSL. The experimental results show that this proposed system accomplishes ranging with an error less than 1mm over a 4-m range.

articleTitle: Fast and Accurate Mapping Method for OPGW Tower Based on M-OTDR
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: This paper describes how distributed optical fiber sensing (DOFS) technology, combined with dark optical fibers within the current optical fiber composite overhead ground wire (OPGW), enables online monitoring and early warning of abnormalities in high-voltage overhead transmission lines. Achieving this goal requires an accurate mapping of the optical cable length to the actual GPS coordinates of the tower. The current tower positioning techniques have drawbacks like low identification rates, high positioning variation, and long calibration times. They are also restricted by particular weather conditions. This study presented a multi-parametric optical time domain reflectance sensing (M-OTDR) system that synchronizes the monitoring of temperature, strain, vibration, and other physical parameters along the fiber optic cable in order to address these problems. Additionally, the study proposed four reference positioning functions. An in-field test was carried out on a 220kV high-voltage transmission line in Fujian Province, PRC. The results showed that the proposed method could guarantee speedy and accurate placement of high-voltage overhead transmission line towers.

Author Keywords: multi-parametric optical time domain reflectance sensing

articleTitle: Numerical Investigation of 2 μm all Polarizationmaintaining Mode-Locked Fiber Laser
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Ultrafast 2 µm all polarization-maintaining figure-9 thulium-doped fiber laser is numerically investigated, and the mode-locking operation region in a weak asymmetrical structure is analyzed that is consistent with the calculated results by Jones matrix method.

articleTitle: Broadband Wavelength Conversion for Mode-Division-Multiplexing Signals in a Width-Modulated Quasi-Phase-Matching Multimode Silicon Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A broadband wavelength conversion method for mode-division-multiplexing (MDM) signals is proposed in a width-modulated multimode silicon waveguide. The quasi-phase-matching (QPM) conditions of four-wave mixing (FWM) processes are met simultaneously for the fundamental and first-order transverse electric modes (TE0 and TE1) by altering the waveguide width periodically. With a 200-mW continuous-wave pump at 1550 nm, the MDM conversion bandwidth is numerically predicted to be over 100 nm with the peak efficiencies of -22 dB for the TE0 mode and -24.5 dB for the TE1 mode, respectively.

articleTitle: Frequency-Tunable Microwave Based on Brillouin Laser Frequency Comb
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We demonstrate a frequency-tunable microwave in a highly stable state. The combination of four-wave mixing, stimulated Brillouin scattering, frequency shifting optical injection locking, and modulation sideband optical injection locking ensures high quality of the microwave signal.

articleTitle: Flexible Fiber Bragg Grating Array for Robotic Finger Tactile Sensing
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A flexible Fiber Bragg grating array for robotic finger tactile sensing is presented. The sensor array is embedded in a PDMS elastomer, which can be attached on a robotic finger for discriminately monitoring the normal force, left force, right force and temperature. The force can be monitored by measure the reflected intensity variation of the three FBGs while temperature can be monitored by measure the wavelength shift of the FBGs.

articleTitle: Single-Polarization Hollow Core Antiresonant Fiber with Nested Cladding Tubes
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A novel single-polarization hollow core anti-resonant fiber (ARF) made of six nested cladding tubes is designed. Through adopting different cladding structure along two orthogonal directions, y-polarized fundamental mode (FM) is effectively confined in the fiber core with lower transmission loss. Meanwhile, the coupling between x-polarized FM and cladding mode (CM) is enhanced near <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${1}{{.55\ \mu m}}$</tex> and results in larger loss. Then the single polarization ARF is achieved and the polarization loss ratio (PLR) reaches to 1083 at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${1}{{.55\ \mu m}}$</tex>. In addition, this ARF has broadband single-polarization region (PLR > 100) in the range of 1.535 ∼ 1.560 μm. The designed ARF deliver excellent performance in near-infrared band and has large commercial potential.

articleTitle: A Machine Learning-Based Indoor Visible Light Positioning System
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: An indoor visible light three-dimensional positioning system with the improved particle swarm optimization (IPSO)-extreme learning machine (ELM) network is proposed in this work, which is optimized by the kernel principal component analysis (KPCA).

articleTitle: CycleGAN-Based Data Augmentation for Enhancing Classification Accuracy in Φ-OTDR Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: This paper proposes a data augmentation method based on CycleGAN to address the problem of classification accuracy being affected by noise and data scarcity in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Phi$</tex>-OTDR systems. The method converts <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Phi$</tex>-OTDR signals into Mel-spectrograms, uses CycleGAN to generate new samples for scarce data categories, and then trains an AlexNet classifier on the augmented dataset. Experiments show this approach can effectively improve classification performance. Additionally, the CycleGAN-based style transfer helps retain original features, providing a new solution for Φ-OTDR's data challenges.

articleTitle: Numerical Study of Helical Multicore Fiber Based Shape Sensing with Arbitrary Twist Distribution
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A comprehensive numerical method is developed based on rotational minimum frames to analyze the helical multicore fiber with specific geometry for 3D shape sensing. The method can simulate the strain distributions along each fiber core while bending and twisting occurs at arbitrary positions. Utilizing a Frenet-Serret formulas derived method for bending and twist discrimination, the shape of the fiber was reconstructed. Additionally, the reconstruction errors were analyzed. The results have shown that our approach not only explores the effectiveness of decoupling-based reconstruction algorithms for bending and twisting but can also be utilized to investigate the influence of fiber geometric parameters such as helical pitch and core spacing to the 3D shape reconstruction.

articleTitle: Focusing Characteristics Of Polarimetric Mixed Eccentric Phase Modulated Linearly Polarized Hyperbolic Cosine-Gaussian Beams
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A polarization-mixed eccentric phase modulated hyperbolic cosine-Gaussian vortex beam is designed. The effects of eccentricity parameter, polarization parameter, phase turning parameter and beam parameter on beam focusing characteristics are discussed in detail by Matlab simulation calculation.

articleTitle: Ultrafast Integrated Automatic Polarization Controller Based on Silicon Photonics
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We realized a silicon automatic polarization controller with a tracking speed up to 105 krad/s, which is the fastest integrated polarization controller to date, through a novel thermal tuning scheme and an advanced control algorithm.

articleTitle: Two-way time comparison based on the phase-derived method
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: This paper proposes a method for two-way time comparison based on phase-derived ranging. Firstly, the relative time difference from site A to B and that from site B to A are accurately measured based on the phase-derived method. Then the precise clock error is calculated according to the symmetric property of the fiber link, so that the two-way time comparison is realized. Through a 100-m fiber link, the errors of two-way time comparison are smaller than 25 ps.

articleTitle: Identification of Soft Failure in Laser Frequency Stability for Coherent Point-to-multipoint Passive Optical Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We propose a DSP based scheme aided by machine learning for soft failure detection oflaser frequency stability. Simulation results demonstrate the high accuracy of identifying abnormal ONUs and estimating frequency drift.

articleTitle: Research on High-impedance Characteristics of Coplanar Waveguide Electrodes in Photodiodes
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A new high-impedance electrode design method is proposed, and after matching the electrodes, a 122ph inductor can be introduced through an 83.45 Ω photodiode electrode impedance, increasing the bandwidth from the original 41 GHz to 69.8 GHz, and the bandwidth enhancement effect is obvious.

articleTitle: Linearized Microwave Photonic Image-Reject Mixer Based On Polarization Multiplexing
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A linearized microwave photonic image-reject mixer (IRM) based on polarization multiplexing is proposed and experimentally verified in this paper. The simultaneous image-reject mixing and the third-order intermodulation distortion (IMD3) suppression are experimentally achieved. The image-reject ratio of 27 dB over 1-GHz bandwidth is achieved. Meanwhile, the SFDR of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{112}\ \mathbf{dB}\cdot \mathbf{Hz}^{\mathbf{2}/\mathbf{3}}$</tex> is realized.

articleTitle: Research on Single Tube Packaging Technology for High-Power Blue Semiconductor Lasers
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A study was conducted on high-power blue semiconductor lasers packaged with AlN and SiC heat sinks of different materials through a combination of simulation and experiment. Thermodynamic analysis of semiconductor lasers with different secondary heat sink materials using simulation software. Simulation results show that due to the lower thermal conductivity of AlN material compared to silicon carbide, the thermal expansion coefficient matches GaN better. The highest temperature of the laser packaged with AlN sub heat sink is 21 K higher than that of SiC sub heat sink, and the maximum stress is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.2\times 103$</tex> Gpa lower than that of SiC sub heat sink. Through experiments, it was found that blue light chips packaged with AlN heat sink achieved better optoelectronic parameters, with a maximum optical power of 0.46W higher than SiC heat sink, a slope efficiency of 0.22W/A higher than SiC heat sink, and a thermal resistance of 1.322K/W lower than SiC heat sink. Although SiC material has a higher thermal conductivity and better heat dissipation performance than AlN material, due to the larger difference in thermal expansion coefficient between SiC material and GaN material, larger residual stress is introduced after packaging, resulting in unsatisfactory packaging effect of SiC secondary heat sink. Therefore, when considering the use of secondary heat sink materials with better heat dissipation performance, how to improve the matching of thermal expansion coefficient of secondary heat sink materials with chip materials is also an issue that cannot be ignored.

articleTitle: High-Performance 1×2 Optical Switch Based on $\text{Ge}_{2}\text{Sb}_{2}\text{Se}_{4}\text{Te}_{1}$-Assisted Racetrack Micro-Ring
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A high-performance nonvolatile <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1\times 2$</tex> optical switch based on the periodic structure <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Ge}2\text{Sb}_{2}\mathrm{s}_{\mathrm{e}4}\text{Te}$</tex> (GSST)-assisted racetrack micro-ring is proposed. The proposed on-chip optical switch is crucial to developing nonvolatile Si-GSST hybrid optical switches and realizing reconfigurable photonic systems.

articleTitle: Digital Twin of All Optical AND Logic Gate Based on Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: As a fundamental component of optical signal processing, the normal operation of an all optical logic gate is the foundation for ensuring the operation of all optical networks. Using deep learning methods to model the all optical logic gate can effectively avoid complex physical analysis processes, and trained networks can predict outputs based on inputs. In this paper, we use deep learning bidirectional LSTM algorithm with attention mechanism to model an all optical logic AND gate implemented using SOA-MZI. To ensure that SOA operates within the normal injection current operating range, a training set with injection current as a feature is used to train the bidirectional LSTM algorithm with attention mechanism. The results demonstrate that this algorithm can effectively model all optical logic AND gates by comparing the difference between simulation output and digital twin output. Meanwhile, prior estimation of the normal operating range of the injected current can be performed.

articleTitle: The Small Deformation Assessment of the Integrated Fiber Optic by the Speckle Field Changes Using Siamese Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Optical fibers sensors have various advantages for precise measurements of wide spectra of parameters. Currently, the deep-learning usage enhances the morphological analysis of the specklegram images. In this study, the design of the full-length optical fiber integration with firm pigtails fixation was used. The Siamese neural network with four convolutional and two fullyconnected layers per each tower was built for assessment of the deformation. The non-loaded specimen specklegram as the first input and image of the specklegram at the loaded state as the second input were used. The accuracy of the trained network with three sets of hyperparameters ranged from 77% to 82.8%.

articleTitle: Numerical and Experimental Investigations of Versatile Soliton Molecules in an All-Polarization-maintaining figure-9 fiber laser
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Soliton molecules evolution is numerically and experimentally investigated in an all-polarization-maintaining figure-9 fiber laser, soliton molecules in different bound states can be regulated by changing the small signal gain and/or the waveplate angle.

articleTitle: Cadmium Sulfide Coated Micro-Nano Fiber Optic Sensor for Ammonia Gas Sensing
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Cadmium sulfide coated micro-nano fiber optic sensor has been developed for measuring trace amounts of ammonia gas. Cadmium sulfide is obtained by chemical precipitation method and is dripped onto the surface of the tapered fiber. When the sensor is placed in an environment containing ammonia, ammonia molecules will bind with cadmium sulfide, thereby changing the relative refractive index of the surface of the tapered fiber and causing a redshift in the interference spectrum. The experimental results show that the ammonia sensitivity of the sensor is 10.88pm/ppm. Additionally, the sensor has good selectivity.

articleTitle: The Design and Optimization of Focal Shift in Focusing Grating Mirrors
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: This paper utilizes the rigorous coupled wave analysis (RCWA) method and finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) algorithm to investigate the focal shift of focusing grating mirrors. By designing and optimizing various dimensions, preset focal length, winding number, and other parameters, the focusing effect of the mirror is observed. The results indicate that the phase focus shift is solely dependent on Fresnel number, while lens size, preset focal length, and incident wavelength are influential factors of Fresnel number. Based on this finding, a new guiding parameter FNg is proposed to better guide and optimize the focal shift phenomenon of grating mirrors and further enhance research on this phenomenon.

articleTitle: Design of High-Power Heterogeneously Integrated III-V-on-Silicon Distributed Feedback Lasers
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We designed high-power heterogeneously integrated III-V-on-silicon distributed feedback lasers. The asymmetric grating was introduced onto the silicon waveguide to improve the output power at one side of lasers while maintaining single-mode operation. For heterogeneously integrated quantum well distributed feedback lasers, optimizing the phase-shift position from conventional 0.50 to 0.64, and the duty cycle at one side of the phase-shift from 0.5 to 0.7 with the other side keeping 0.5, the ratio of the optical output power at both sides of lasers is dramatically increased from 1.0 to 7.5, and to 9.2 for heterogeneously integrated quantum dot distributed feedback lasers. This work provides a step forward towards the development of high-power silicon-based light sources.

articleTitle: Numerical Simulations of Spatial Coherence Factors for Interferometric Multimode Speckles
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We described a statistical simulation model for generating heterodyne and homodyne speckles for a multimode interferometry system, which includes a single-mode-based reference arm and a multimode-based sample arm. Based on the generated interferometric multimode speckles, we calculated and compared the heterodyne and homodyne coherence factors under various spatial modal contents.

articleTitle: Realizing Complex Integrated Reconstructive Spectrometers Using Inverse Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A novel inverse design method for integrated reconstructive spectrometer is proposed. This method can lead to optimized and controllable performance of the spectrometer. It is validated on an integrated reconstructive spectrometer consisting of novel components.

articleTitle: Efficient Fluorescence Coupling Integrated Fiber Magnetometer Based on Nitrogen Vacancy Centers
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A magnetic field sensor based on a fiber-optic integrated probe at the center of a nitrogen vacancy (NV) is proposed and demonstrated. Fiber optics are utilized to replace all conventional spatial optics while efficiently enabling laser excitation and fluorescence collection from diamond. Optical models were developed to study the fluorescence collection efficiency of diamond. The fiber-coupled probe was simulated and its efficiency was improved to 3.062% compared to the 0.607% fluorescence coupling efficiency of the fiber. The optical probe magnetic resonance (ODMR) phenomenon was successfully observed and significantly improved the magnetic field sensitivity to 5.3 nT/Hz<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1/2</sup>, which proved the feasibility and performance compared with the conventional confocal NV-centered magnetometer.

articleTitle: Research on a Method of Flow Noise Suppressing for Optical Fiber Hydrophone Towed Array
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A flexible suspension scheme for optical fiber hydrophone towed array is proposed to achieve the effect of noise suppression and to reduce flow noise. By establishing a simulation model, the characteristics of three suspended structure were analyzed, and the effect was verified in the experiment.

articleTitle: Research on Denoising of Second Harmonic Signal in TDLAS Based on BOA-VMD Method
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: This paper proposes and simulates a denoising method of TDLAS second harmonic signal based on butterfly optimization algorithm-variational mode decomposition method, which is used to improve the accuracy of system.

articleTitle: Perturbation-Based Nonlinearity Compensation for Optical Fiber Transmission using BiLSTM
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, a scheme of second-order perturbation-based nonlinearity compensation (SO-PB-NLC) algorithm using bidirectional LSTM (BiLSTM) is proposed and applied for the fiber nonlinearity compensation. After 1200 km transmission, the computational complexity of the proposed algorithm is reduced by 66% compared with the traditional ANN.

articleTitle: Transfer of Multimaterial Nanofilms Based on Hydroxide Catalysis Bonding Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In order to realize the multifunctionality of materials and to promote the application of nanomaterials in various fields, the transfer technology of multi-material nanofilms provides a method for the precise assembly of materials. We report a multi-material nanofilm transfer process based on hydroxide catalysis bonding technology, which can be used to transfer nanoscale thin-film materials such as gold, silver, chromium onto the interface of silica materials, and realize the patterned transfer of gold and silver. The technology provides a method for precise glue-free assembly of materials, where different types of materials can be efficiently integrated, providing more functional options for applications such as electronics and sensors.

articleTitle: Graphere/MoS2 Film Based Optical Fiber Microcavity Relative Humidity Sensor
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: 2-D material film is a good candidate for moisture-sensitive material, especially for the Graphere/MoS2 film. Here, we show our recent research achievement in optical fiber microcavity relative humidity sensor fabricated by laser 3D printing. The inner Graphere/ MoS2 film serves both the reflective surface and moisture-sensitive film of the microcavity. The sensor shows the advantages of high sensitivity, fast response time and good repeatability. It is expected to have wide applications in chemical and medical relative humidity detection areas.

articleTitle: On-Demand Scheduling of Computing Power Resources Based on Deterministic Delay Guarantees
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We propose a scheme that combine service delay requirements with computing resource deployment for on-demand scheduling. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed scheme can reduce blocking ratio and provide deterministic delay for each domain.

articleTitle: Silicon Integrated Computational Spectrometer with Cascaded Add-Drop Micro-Ring Resonators
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We report the design and implementation of an integrated computational spectrometer on a silicon-on-insulator substrate. The device has 31 filter units, which are cascaded add-drop micro-ring resonators with different parameters. The spectrometer has a footprint of 1.5 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>and shows a resolution of 0.11 nm in the C-band.

articleTitle: Low Complexity Blind Phase Search for Coherent Optical Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, a phase noise estimation method called minimum bisection blind phase search (MB-BPS) is proposed. Comparing with original blind phase search (BPS), the result shows that the number of multipliers can be reduced by 48.7% and the adder is also decreased by 47.9% under similar bit error rate (BER) performance.

articleTitle: FSO Technologies for Cellular Mobile Communications
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We delineate a few technical challenges of employing of free-space optical communication technologies for cellular mobile communications and propose potential solutions for the challenges. They include direct impingement of solar irradiance onto the receiver, blockage of the line-of-sight path, and accurate beam alignment.

articleTitle: Multi-Channel Acoustic Detection with Polarization Hole Burning Effect in Multi-Wavelength Erbium-Doped Fiber Laser
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, we propose and demonstrate a novel multi-point sound source localization system utilizing the hole-burning effect in erbium-doped fiber lasers and Fabry-Perot (F-P) sensors for signal reception. The system employs nonlocal mean filtering and empirical mode decomposition algorithms for preprocessing sound signals, effectively filtering external noise while preserving the original signal integrity. The generalized quadratic cross-correlation algorithm is then applied to determine delay differences between adjacent F-P sensors, facilitating precise sound source localization. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach in accurately locating sound sources based on signals received from four sensors.

articleTitle: A High Response Bandwidth DAS System Based on Optical Loop Modulation
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We propose a Distributed acoustic sensing (DAS) system with a high response based on sequential frequency division multiplexing (FDM). Pulse sequences with different frequencies and delays are modulated by an optical loop structure and injected into the sensing fiber. The vibration signals are discretely collected by Rayleigh backscattering light (RBS) signals with different delays and frequencies. After frequency demultiplexing of the RBS signal in the digital domain, the high-fidelity differential phase of the vibration region was extracted using the peak search method and interlacing according to the time delay order to achieve high-dense sampling of the vibration signal. Compared with the traditional sequential frequency division multiplexing scheme, the scheme using an optical loop structure to generate pulse sequence reduces the dependence on the bandwidth performance of the microwave signal source and the modulator, effectively controls the experimental cost, and provides a new scheme for sequential pulse sequence modulation.

articleTitle: Multiparameter Sensing Via Multiresonant Analysis of Tilted Fiber Bragg Grating
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We propose and experimentally demonstrate a multiparameter sensing method based on multiresonant analysis of a tilted fiber Bragg grating (TFBG). With a calibrated gauge factor matrix, the multiparameter sensing of temperature, strain, and surrounding refractive index is achieved by a single TFBG.

articleTitle: The Design and Simulation of High-order OAM Mode Couplers
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We propose a fiber coupler that supports 7-order orbital angular momentum (OAM) modes with adjustable coupling efficiency. The coupler is composed of an OAM air-core fiber (ACF) and a single mode fiber (SMF) that are side-polished. The high mode field distribution and effective index of the ACF are calculated based on the beam propagation method (BPM). At the wavelength of 1500nm, phase matching between the fundamental mode and specific modes in the ACF is achieved by appropriate tapering of the single mode. The launched fundamental mode <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{LP}_{\mathbf{01}}$</tex> couples to the higher order modes <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathbf{OAM}_{\mathbf{7},\mathbf{1}})$</tex> with coupling efficiency over 90%. Additionally, in order to achieve effective excitation of the 7-order OAM mode and flexible adjustment of coupling efficiency, we discuss the effects of coupling length and core-core pitch on coupling efficiency and coupling mode. The proposed mode coupler is expected to find potential applications in all-fiber optical signal processing, multiplexing and sensing systems.

articleTitle: Research on the Cascaded KP4 and Zipper Codes Based on Optimized Sliding Window Decoder
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We adopt a novel structure of cascaded KP4 and zipper codes based on optimized sliding window decoder. By optimizing the hard-decision decoder and interleaver length, the pre-FEC BER threshold of error-free transmission is approximately 0.7E-2.

articleTitle: Time Domain Demodulation Algorithm for Current Transformers Based on Saganc Interferometer
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Based on the characteristics of optical couplers, a time domain demodulation algorithm for Sagnac Interferometer current transformers is proposed, which can reduce external interference and is insensitive to the polarization state of the input light.

articleTitle: Llama-Log: Optical Network Log Parsing with Fine-Tuned Large Language Model
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: This study proposes a method that involves finetuning the open-source large language model Llama2 for the task of parsing optical network logs. Through comparative experiments, we have validated the effectiveness of this method.

articleTitle: Mode Transformation Of Multipole Beams with Orbital Angular Momentum
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The transmission characteristics of a quadrupole beam with a novel orbital angular momentum is investigated. The rotational mode transformation of this beam during transmission in strongly nonlocal nonlinear materials is analyzed and illustrated.

articleTitle: Sleep Efficiency Monitoring Based on Fiber MZI Sensor Mattress
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We used the mattress embedded with a Mach-Zehener interferometer(MZI) fiber optic sensor to collect the physiological signals during sleep, extracted the sleep features after filtering the original signals to calculate the sleep efficiency.

articleTitle: Advanced ROPA Scheme for Unrepeatered 100G Transmission System
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: This paper reviews the current progress in Remote Optical Pumped Amplifier (ROPA) technology for 100Gb/s unrepeatered transmission systems in recent years. Building on the existing extensive deployment of G.652.D standard optical fibers, an optimized ROPA structure combined with distributed Raman amplifiers has been utilized, achieving real-time transmission of 40x 100Gb/s over a distance of 383 km(76.8dB span loss).

articleTitle: Real Time Time-Frequency Transmission System Based on Multi-Core Optical Fibers
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We propose a high-precision multi-core fiber time-frequency synchronization scheme based on FPGA. The experimental results shows that time synchronization accuracy is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm$</tex> 31.71ps, time stability is 1. <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0413\text{ps/s}$</tex>, and transmission frequency stability is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3.3076\times 10^{-16}/\mathrm{s}$</tex>.

articleTitle: Research on Automatic Identification of FBGs Being Forced Laterally in Series Connection with 3 FBGs
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: This paper presents a method for automatic identification of FBGs being forced laterally in series connection. 3 FBGs with different Bragg wavelengths are connected through series connection, and are forced laterally, then the spectra are recorded and compared. Based on the comparing data one kind of program identification method to judge the FBG being forced laterally is constructed. The program's output is corresponding with the actual situation very well.

articleTitle: Temperature Response Analysis of Intelligent OPPC Cable Core Based on Finite Element Simulation
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The Optical Fiber Composite Overhead Conductor (OPPC) cable is a special type of power optical cable that combines overhead conductor and communication capabilities. It has advantages such as strong wind resistance, good corrosion resistance, high bandwidth transmission, low loss transmission, and high reliability. However, as the OPPC cable operates for a long time power transmission, its long-term working temperature has a significant impact on transmission performance and lifespan. Therefore, monitoring the temperature of the OPPC cable and internal fibers can improve the transmission capacity of the line, ensure good thermal stability, and provide important references for fault warning and maintenance. This study aims to explore the temperature characteristics of the OPPC cable through actual monitoring and analysis, providing guidance and decision-making basis for practical applications.

articleTitle: A Spectral-Efficient Coherent RoF Link for 5G Millimeter-Wave Transmission
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A spectral-efficient radio over fiber (RoF) link transmitting two millimeter-wave vector signals at the same frequency is proposed and verified by simulations. At the transmitter, two millimeter-wave vector signals are respectively modulated on the intensity and phase of the optical carrier through a dual-parallel Mach-Zehnder modulator (DPMZM). By mixing with a three-line optical frequency comb, the two millimeter-wave signals are photonically down-converted and detected. After simple digital signal processing, the laser phase fluctuation between the two lasers is eliminated and the two signals are separated and demodulated respectively. In simulations, two 16-QAM microwave vector signals with a symbol rate of 100 Msym/s at 25 GHz are transmitted over 25 km single-mode fiber (SMF). The error vector magnitudes (EVMs) of the recovered signals are 8.28% and 7.6%. The channel isolation over 20 dB is obtained for each signal transmission.

articleTitle: Demonstration of Photonic Sub-THz ISAC System with Real-Time 251.03-Gbps Communication Rate and Offline 2.5-cm Sensing Resolution
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The intelligence of future society necessitates an immediate requirement for ultra-high-speed communication and ultra-resolution sensing in the 6G era. In this demonstration, we present a photonic sub-THz integrated sensing and communication system. The demonstrated system achieves a real-time line rate of 251.03 Gbps and an offline sensing resolution of 2.5 cm, resulting in an impressive capacity-resolution quotient of up to 100.41 Gbps/cm. The ultra-high-speed real-time communication is based on a fiber-THz-fiber transmission architecture, which boasts ultra-wideband real-time processing capability. Meanwhile, the ultra-resolution sensing is accomplished utilizing an optical frequency comb with low frequency offset and low phase noise.

articleTitle: Nonlinear Compensation Based on Bidirectional Temporal Convolutional Network in Underwater Visible Light Communication System
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this work, we proposed a Bidirectional Temporal Convolutional network (BiTCN) model to process signal post-equalization in underwater visible light communication channel (UVLC) for the first time. This strategy is more resistant to nonlinearities compared to traditional equalizers like least mean square (LMS) equalizer and avoids the inefficiency issue caused by the sequential processing requirement of Bidirectional Gate Recurrent Unit (BiGRU) networks, through this approach, we successfully conduct a transmission of a 64quadrature amplitude modulation-carrierless amplitude (64QAM-CAP) signal in a 1.2m underwater experiment using a blue laser operating at a wavelength of 450 nm. Remarkably, our system achieves a high data rate of 16.2 Gbps, all while maintaining the bit error rate (BER) below the 7% hard decision forward error correction (HD-FEC) threshold of 3.8E-3. Under optimal Peak-to-Peak Voltages (VPP) and bias current conditions, compared to the post equalization methods of LMS+Volterra and BiGRU, our proposed method achieved speed improvements of 550 and 210 Mbps, respectively.

articleTitle: CNN Based Equalizer in NFDM System with B-Modulation
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A CNN-based equalization scheme is proposed, and experimentally verified in 14.4 Gbps-16QAM NFDM optical communication system with 1600 km. The result shows that at LOP=-7.1dBm, the BER decreases by ~50.7<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>.

articleTitle: Power Control with Online Gain Optimization for Multi-Band Optical Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We briefly overview power management technologies in multi-band optical networks and proposed a power control method with online gain optimization. Experimental results show the effectiveness of proposed method in both power equalization and transmission optimization.

articleTitle: ZUC-256 High Throughput FPGA Implementation
