publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The ZUC-256 algorithm is a stream encryption algorithm. In this paper, we have successfully achieved a throughput of 13.33 Gbit/s on FPGA. Our experiment has provided more possibilities for physical layer encryption.

articleTitle: Numerical Analysis of Photonic Lanterns for the Fabrication via Pull-cone and 3D Printing
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We numerically analyze the forming of photonic lantern by using traditional pull-cone and 3D printing fabrication methodology. The results show that the 3D printed photonic lantern has better performance in mode conversion in the calculation.

articleTitle: A Multi-Agent Routing Algorithm with Trajectory Prediction for Highly Dynamic UAV Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: To address the routing problems in high-dynamic UAV networks, a multi-agent routing algorithm with trajectory prediction is proposed. Simulations show the proposed algorithm can achieve better performance on the end-to-end delay and packet delivery ratio.

articleTitle: Novel Meandering Coplanar Waveguide Electrodes for Enhancing the Bandwidth of Avalanche Photodiode
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel meandering coplanar waveguide electrode to enhance the bandwidth of avalanche photodiodes (APDs). Simulation results indicate that the bandwidth of APD with the proposed electrode can increase by 113%. (Abstract)

articleTitle: A Calibration Method for Linear Displacement Sensors Based on Operating Temperature
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The output of high-precision linear displacement sensors is sensitive to environmental temperature, and during their use, there are situations where the operating temperature deviates from the calibration temperature. To study the metrology traceability method of linear displacement sensors at operating temperature, a calibration device for linear displacement sensors at operating temperature without damaging the traceability conditions was proposed. A thermostatic box was used to simulate the operating temperature of the sensor, and a laser interferometer was used as the measurement standard. The measurement range of the calibration device is (0–200) mm. The calibration experiment of the sensor was conducted using this device, and the results showed that the device can track the output of the sensor at different temperatures. The measurement uncertainty of this method was evaluated, and the results showed that the expanded measurement uncertainty of the basic error calibration results of the linear displacement sensor was better than 0.06%.

articleTitle: Sensitivity Enhancement of Fiber-Optic Curvature Sensor
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, we report a fiber-optic curvature sensor by the tapering splicing based on the seven-core-fiber Mach-Zehnder interferometer(t-SCF-MZI). The light field distributions are researched by beam propagation method with the varied diameters of taper waist. The results are experimentally gained that the curvature response of t-SCF-MZI is significantly enhanced owing to varied taper diameter. Under a sequence of experiments, ~200% improvement of curvature sensitivity is obtained and the maximum reaches -30.647nm/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup>with the tapered diameter of 41.44 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu\mathrm{m}$</tex>, Due to the merits of susceptible fabrication and low cost, the proposed sensor is quite practical and prospective for high-precision curvature-related engineering monitoring.

articleTitle: Observation of Bound Noise-Like Pulses in an Yb-Doped Fiber Laser
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Dynamically bound noise-like pulses as a kind of optical soliton molecular complexes have been produced directly from a mode-locked Yb-doped fiber laser. This demonstration reveals the existence of a new form of pulse bound state and further enriches the variety of pulse dynamic patterns. The numerical predictions are consistent with the experimental observations.

articleTitle: A Broadband Achromatic Terahertz Metalens
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: This article presents the design of an achromatic terahertz metalens that operates within the frequency range of 0.8 THz to 1.2 THz. Simulation results verify that the proposed superlens can effectively eliminate chromatic aberration.

articleTitle: Low-Latency Frequency Division Multiplexing Using Entropy Loading for Multi-Point-to-Point Passive Optical Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We experimentally demonstrate a low-latency frequency division multiplexing using entropy loading for multi-point-to-point passive optical networks, where optical network units can achieve a similar bit error rate below the 20% soft decision-forward error correction limit.

articleTitle: Temperature Monitoring and Electrical Fault Warning Methods of Three-Core Submarine Cables
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The study establishes the correlation between conductor temperature and optical fiber temperature under various conditions. It was observed that during a single-phase short circuit, the conductor temperature can rapidly rise to 247°C within 1 second. The cable temperature exceeds 250°C in less than a second when load currents surpass the rated load current. Furthermore, simulations of temperature distribution during a leakage fault revealed that the variation and rise rate of optical fiber temperature in submarine cables can effectively detect and assess the severity of the leakage. These temperature changes also serve as indicators of the average discharge power, adding another parameter for monitoring. Utilizing the BOTDR method proves to be a reliable approach for online monitoring of submarine cable faults. By monitoring temperature changes and the rise rate of optical modules, prompt detection and resolution of leakage faults are ensured, thus maintaining the safety and efficiency of submarine cables.

articleTitle: High Sensitivity Magnetic Field Sensor Composed of Magnetostrictive Material Terfenol-D and Fabry-Perot Interferometer
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A highly sensitive magnetic field sensor was proposed using magnetostrictive material Terfenol-D and Fabry-Perot interferometer (FPI) and experimental verification was conducted. Ordinary single-mode fiber are fusion spliced together with quartz capillary, and then a layer of PVA film is coated on the end face of the capillary to form an FPI. Then, the FPI structure is glued onto the end face of the Terfenol-D rod using UV adhesive to form a magnetic field sensor. When the external magnetic field changes, the Terfenol-D rod will stretch and contract, causing a change in the F-P cavity length of the FPI pasted together, resulting in a shift in the resonant wavelength of the FPI spectrum. By demodulating the wavelength shift, the magnetic field size can be obtained. The magnetic field sensitivity of the sensor obtained in the experiment reached -0.5172 nm/mT, with a fitting degree of 0.9959. In addition, magnetic field sensors have good stability and repeatability, and respond quickly.

articleTitle: Research on Image Recognition and Classification of Weld Defects Based on Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The algorithm of median filter as well as bottom cap transform is used for defect identification. The improved training accuracy and test accuracy are 96.24% and 90%, which can meet industrial production requirements.

articleTitle: A Dynamic Computing Power Scheduling Scheme for the EDWC Project in China
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, we conduct the cost analysis of the EDWC project. Studies show the current transmission cost is too high. We present a scheme to schedule the computing jobs based on the price fluctuation.

Author Keywords: Eastern Data and Western Computing project

articleTitle: Shape Sensing Using In-Fiber Thermally Diffused Coupler and Fiber Bragg Gratings
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A multi-core optical fiber shape sensor based on inscribing fiber Bragg gratings core-by-core was proposed. A coupler was fabricated utilizing thermal diffusion technology to facilitate single-channel measurement of multi-core fiber Bragg gratings.

articleTitle: Inverse Design of Compact Silicon Dual-mode Demultiplexer and Power Splitter
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We report the inverse design and demonstration of silicon dual-mode demultiplexer and power splitter with footprints of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3.88\times 2.35\mu \mathrm{m}^{2}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$5.4\times 5.4\mu \mathrm{m}^{2}$</tex>, respectively. The demultiplexer shows a measured insertion loss of 0.5 dB and an inter-mode crosstalk of −13.2 dB at 1550 nm. The dual-mode power splitter has an excess loss of 1.1 dB and an inter-mode crosstalk of −22.4 dB at 1550 nm.

articleTitle: Research on Strawberry Fruit Detection Based on YOLOv7
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Strawberries is a popular fruit, and reliable detection is critical for modern agriculture. The article utilizes YOLOv7 for fruit detection and ripeness assessment, demonstrating promising outcomes, indicative of enhanced agricultural efficiency and sustain ability.

articleTitle: Research on Salinity Detection Sensors Based on Scanning Taper and Fixed Point Taper Micro/Nanofiber
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: This paper introduced a salinity sensor based on scanning and fixed point taper. Experiments encompassed fibers with varying diameters (2.0 μm, 1.6 μm, 1.4 μm, 1.0 μm) and lengths (80,000 μm, 22,500 μm). The scanning taper approach demonstrated superior sensitivity, with a theoretical sensitivity of 0.501 dB/% closely mirrored by an experimental sensitivity of 0.495 dB/%. It was characterized by precision, an extensive detection spectrum, and enhanced mitigation of temperature interference, this sensor was particularly well-suited for applications in marine environments.

articleTitle: Multi-Mode Multiplexing Reservoir Computing Based on a WRC-FPLD with Optical Feedback
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We proposed and numerically investigated a multi-mode multiplexing parallel task processing reservoir computing system based on a WRC-FPLD under delay optical feedback. The simulated results show that the best parallel processing performance (NMSE=0.029) can be achieved under some optimized operation parameters.

articleTitle: Tapered Single-Mode Optical Fiber pH Sensor Coated with Hydrogel Working at the Dispersion Turning Point
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A pH sensor based on the dispersion turning point (DTP) is proposed, with a structure involving a thin layer of calcium alginate hydrogel coated on a tapered single-mode fiber (SMF). The tapered SMF with a waist diameter of 3.85 μm and a length of 7000 μm is fabricated using a two-step tapering method. Experimental results indicate that the sensitivity of the sensor to pH values ranging from 7.03 to 8.45 is 58.11 nm/pH. The pH sensor we proposed features high sensitivity, low cost, and simple fabrication process, among other advantages.

articleTitle: Vector Bending Sensor Based on 3D Printed Seven Core Fiber
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A novel vector bending sensor is proposed based on 3D printed seven core fiber (SCF). There are two sensing elements in the proposed sensor. One is the fiber Bragg grating (FBG) inscribed in the 3D printed SCF, and the other is the Mach-Zehnder interferometer (MZI) with the structure of single-mode fiber (SMF)-SCF-SMF. Two sensing elements exhibit significantly different responses to bending. In the curvature range of 1.115 to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M^{-1}$</tex>, the curvature sensitivity of the MZI element is 22.622 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$nm/M^{-1}$</tex>, while that of the FBG element is 0.044 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$nm/M^{-1}$</tex> in the same direction. Especially, due to the asymmetrical structure of 3D printed SCF, the proposed bending sensor clearly displays directional dependence. Given to the flexible design and manufacture of 3D printed fiber in structure and material, this study demonstrates that 3D printing fiber technology brings more opportunities for the development of advanced fiber sensors in future Internet of Things.

articleTitle: On-Chip Implementation of Intelligent Signal Recognition in Fiber-Optic DAS
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The accelerator implementation method of intelligent signal recognition is proposed for fiber-optic DAS in this paper. The processing time can achieve at 0.398ms on the FPGA platform of ZCU102 for the signal at each fiber sensing node, which is equivalent to 0.7212s for a total fiber length of 18.7km with a spatial resolution of 10.32m. This processing time is much faster than 3.47ms and 6.288s on the desktop workstation (CPU:13400, Memory:16G) for one node and the whole monitoring line respectively. With this significant increase in the processing speed, the recognition accuracy for four types of real field events can achieve at as high as 97.37% on FPGA, which is only 0.81 % lower than that on CPU, while the maximum power consumption is only 25W, which is just 1/6 of the typical operating power for CPU. It provides a fast, accurate and power efficient on-chip processing solution for various safety monitoring applications of DAS.

articleTitle: Space-Time Coordinated Scheduling Approach in Computing Power Optical Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, an STC-SnF approach is presented to schedule bulk data transfers across the CPON. Studies show it can ensure the coordinated space-time relation of bandwidth fragments and hence benefit the SnF scheduling process.

articleTitle: Vortex Fiber Laser Based on Twisted High Concentration Doped Active Fiber
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We demonstrated a linear-cavity vortex laser by twisting a homemade highly doped active fiber, which can generate stable vortex beams, and the output power of the laser can reach up to 22.5 mW.

articleTitle: Waveguide Amplifiers in SiN Photonics Heterogeneous Integration with Er:Yb:TeO2 thin films
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A heterogeneous optical amplifier is proposed and present in an alternative silicon nitride (SiN) waveguide via integration with an erbium-ytterbium co-doped tellurium oxide layer. This work provides an efficient and innovative strategy to implement SiN-based integrated waveguide amplifiers.

articleTitle: Interference Cancellation and Iterative Multi-User Detection for Satellite OTFS-NOMA Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: An iterative multiuser detection based on channel matched filtering and interference cancellation is proposed for satellite-terrestrial OTFS-NOMA systems. Simulation results demonstrate that our algorithm effectively mitigates inter-user and inter-symbol interference, accurately detecting all superposed signals.

articleTitle: Embedded Flexible Shape Cable for Marine Exploit Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: An embedded flexible shape cable has been first proposed and the verification of real-time shape measurement has been achieved. It is produced by sequentially preparing shape sensing units, shape sensing optical cables, and optoelectronic composite cables. Temperature has little effect on shape reconstruction over a long period of time, and the end stability is less than 0.012m. Real-time shape measurement is achieved in both vertical and horizontal directions within a range of 4.5 m. The curvature measurement accuracy is 0.05 m1 and the shape reconstruction errors are 3.0% and 1.7%, respectively. The flexible shape cables can be used for shape monitoring in areas such as power transmission cables between islands and flexible pipeline cables for offshore oil and gas resource extraction, improving the safety of marine resource development.

articleTitle: A SnF Scheduling Method for HFL Over Edge Computing Power Optical Network
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A SnF scheduling method is presented to schedule data transfers in the HFL aggregation process across the ECPON. Studies demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms conventional methods in terms of network performance and training accuracy.

articleTitle: An Automatic Multiplexing Circular Polarimetric Instrument for High-Sensitive Pathological Diagnosis of Ischemic Stroke
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The future of pathology is automatic and digital. Here, a label-free, sensitive, and rapid circular polarimetric method is proposed for assisting the brain tissue sections' disease digital pathology. In addition, the entire system is integrated as an automatic instrument. The unattended automatic detection provides diagnosis advice by measuring the polarization metrics of forward-scattering light from tissue. The depolarization shows indication at diseased tissue. Finally, a newly designed multiplexing optical fiber meta-tip is adopted and achieves an ultra-high accuracy.

articleTitle: Effects of Random Birefringence in Multimode Fibers on Nonlinear Beam Self-cleaning
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Based on a proposed theoretical model, the spatial beam self-cleaning in multimode fibers with random birefringence are analyzed, and the beam self-cleaning is found to resist the random birefringence at high input peak power.

articleTitle: Simultaneous Measurement of Temperature and Refractive Index Using an Ellipsoidal Extrinsic Fabry- Perot Interferometer
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A novel ellipsoidal extrinsic Fabry-Perot interferometer (EEFPI) -based sensor is proposed and demonstrated. The experimental results show the sensor has a refractive index (RI) sensitivity of 77.01 dB/RIU for RI ranging at 1.3350-1.3660, while the temperature sensitivity is 225 pm/°C from 30-60°C. The excellent merits such as easy fabrication and miniature size make the proposed sensor has a potential application in the field of biochemical.

articleTitle: A GSST Functionalized Microring Resonant Cavity for Photonic Memory
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We propose a novel nonvolatile photonic on-chip memory, and demonstrate a 9-level coded memory based on a GSST sandwich slot ring resonator that can encode information in real time by using a process of modulation pulses to induce a nonvolatile phase transition in GSST.

articleTitle: Double-Layer Secure Optical Communication System Incorporating Chaotic Encryption and Signal Covert Transmission
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A double-layer secure optical communication system incorporating chaotic encryption and signal covert transmission is proposed. In this system, 10 Gb/s data is encrypted using a shared key and transmitted stealthily over the public signal, making it undetectable to eavesdroppers.

articleTitle: Computing and Spectrum Resource Collaborative Allocation Strategy in Computing Power Optical Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We propose an RQ-RCSA computing power routing and spectrum resource collaborative allocation strategy in computing power optical networks. Simulation results indicate that it can achieve low blocking ratio and high resource utilization.

Author Keywords: Collaborative Allocation of Computing and Spectrum Resources

articleTitle: AN-D2NN: Classification of Modes with Amplitude Nonlinear Diffractive Deep Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: This study introduces an amplitude-nonlinear diffractive deep neural network (AN-D2NN), which enhances LP mode classification accuracy. A three-layer AN-D2NN demonstrates superiority optimized by reinforcement learning. Experimental results confirm exceptional performance with 98.7% accuracy.

articleTitle: Enhancement of Manhole Low-Light Images Based on Improved EnlightenGAN
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: This paper presents a manhole image enhancement technique, establishing a low-light image enhancement network based on an improved EnlightenGAN model. This method effectively enhances the illumination and contrast of manhole images.

articleTitle: Dispersion Compensating Fiber for OAM Modes
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Fibers with multiple concentric-ring regions designed for compensating OAM modes dispersion are summarized. It details the optical characteristics of OAM modes supported in dual-ring-core fibers and introduces PCFs and triple ring-core fibers with similar principles.

articleTitle: Design of Flat and Spiral Phase Plates for Vortex Beam Generation for 3D Printing Purpose
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We present a study of flat and spiral phase plates for vortex beam generation, which serves for 3D printing purposes. Vortex beams topological charges are determined by refractive index and height of the phase plates.

articleTitle: Femtosecond Laser Inscribed Bragg Gratings in Planar Lightwave Circuit with Low Polarization-Dependent Loss
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: This paper investigates the influence of femtosecond laser polarization on the performance of polarization-dependent loss of the Bragg gratings inscribed in a planar lightwave circuit. After optimization, a high-quality Bragg grating in planar lightwave circuit is prepared with a low polarization-dependent loss of 2.42 dB.

articleTitle: A Fiber Optic Temperature and Strain Sensor Based on Few-Mode Fiber Grating
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The paper proposes a less-mode fiber grating dual-parameter sensor to eliminate cross-sensitivity. The sensor demonstrates temperature and strain sensitivities of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$11\text{pm}/{}^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1.06 \text{pm} /\mu \varepsilon$</tex>, respectively.

articleTitle: Experimental Demonstration of Power over Fiber for Power Grid Application
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, we experimentally demonstrate the standard single mode fiber based PoF system with 10W optical power and 155 Mb/s data rate transmitted simultaneously over 1 km. The high-speed data signal is generated from an commercial optical module with combination of the optical switch applied in the Power Grid infrastructure. The experimental results show the potential application of PoF technology for Power Grid to provide the the low-power consumption inline performance monitoring or electrical power supply under emergency rescue etc.

articleTitle: RL-based Bandwidth Decision in Optical Access Networks: When to Exploit a Decision with Confidence? (Invited)
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: This paper reviews our recent study of when reinforcement-learnt bandwidth decisions can be exploited with trust to reduce latency in optical access networks. We introduce Reward Variance-Oriented (RVO) learning strategy that drives provable confident decisions in the least time.

articleTitle: FPGA-Based Multi-Pulse Laser Ranging System
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: This paper designs an FPGA-based laser ranging system that achieves high-precision distance measurement of 2 km with a ranging error of less than 20 cm by utilizing wavelet transform and multi-pulse stacking.

articleTitle: Spectrally Efficient Faster-Than-Nyquist Dual-Band Transmission Enabled by Inter-Subcarrier Crosstalk Cancellation
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We propose and experimentally demonstrate an inter-subcarrier crosstalk cancellation algorithm for fasterthan-Nyquist transmission. At 20% HD-FEC threshold, the achievable faster-than-Nyquist rate improves from 0.875 to 0.8 for 16-QAM and from 0.75 to 0.6 for QPSK.

articleTitle: Microwave photonic radar with flexible tuning multiband LFM signal generation
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, a tunable multiband linear frequency modulation (LFM) microwave photonic radar system is proposed. The system simultaneously generates linear frequency modulation signals at three frequency bands with two different chirp rates. The center frequencies of the generated signals can be easily tuned from the L to K band. Target detection in different frequency bands is implemented experimentally with a distance measurement error of less than 2.5 cm and a range resolution of 3.9 cm,

articleTitle: Experimental and Theoretical Analysis of Deep Residual Time-Delay Reservoir Computing Based on Clipping Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Photonic reservoir computing (RC), as a crucial variant of recurrent neural networks, has boasted substantial potential owing to its straightforward training processes and facile hardware integration. In this work, we introduce and validate both experimentally and numerically a novel post-processing technique, referred to as the clipping algorithm (CA), utilized on the high-performance deep residual time-delay RC (DR-TDRC). The proof-of-concept model, i.e., a four-layer DR-TDRC, comprises 960 interrelated neurons (240 neurons per layer) based on four injection-locked distributed feedback lasers. Our results demonstrate that the implementation of the CA can effectively mitigate issues associated with the redundant layers and improve the performance of deep architectures.

articleTitle: Carboxyl-Free Synthesis of Red InP/ZnSe/ZnSeS/ZnS Quantum Dots with Narrow Full Width at Half Maximum
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: InP based quantum dots are a new type of fluorescent nanomaterials, which have a very promising potential to replace heavy metal contained quantum dots such as Cd-based ones due to their low toxicity and environmentally friendly properties. In this paper, ZnCl2 instead of zinc carboxylate was chosen as the zinc source, and low-cost and low-toxicity tris(dimethylamino)phosphine) (DMA)3P was used as the phosphorus source, red-emitting InP/ZnSe/ZnSeS/ZnS quantum dots with a narrow full width at half maximum (44 nm) and a photoluminescence quantum yield (PLQY) of 73% were synthesized using a one-pot method.

Author Keywords: narrow full width at half maximum

articleTitle: A Machine Vision Method for Washbasin Cutting
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: This paper presents a machine vision method for automated basin cutting. It quickly acquires contours, addresses occlusions, and achieves high automation using a Surface Fitting Algorithm. The machine vision method developed in this paper has been tested and proven to meet practical production requirements with an error tolerance of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm \mathbf{0.1}\mathbf{mm}$</tex>. Compared to previous production methods, it has significantly reduced the time consumption to 40%. It reduces manual involvement and meets industrial demands effectively.

articleTitle: Research and Discussion on Digital Twin Architecture of 5G Bearer Network
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Based on the research of digital twin technology in the field of information communication, this paper mainly proposes the architecture of digital twin for 5G bearer network, and the deployment strategy of digital twin technology in 5G bearer network is also discussed.

articleTitle: The research focuses on the development of a measurement method for liquid film on fuel rods based on reflective optical fiber sensor
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We presented a novel sensor for liquid film thickness on fuel rods based on reflective fiber sensing. It can withstand the temperature of 350°C, measure range is 1.5mm, and accuracy can reach the micron level.

articleTitle: Intensity-Interrogated Hot-Wire Anemometer Based on Narrow-Linewidth Laser and Cobalt-Doped Fiber Bragg Grating
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: An intensity-interrogated optical fiber hot-wire anemometer employing a cobalt-doped fiber (CDF) based fiber Bragg grating (FBG) is proposed. The CDF-FBG is heated and turned into a hot wire by using a high-power laser whose energy is absorbed by the CDF. In the presence of airflow, temperature of the CDF-FBG decreases with airflow velocity, causing wavelength blue-shift of the CDF-FBG. A narrow-linewidth laser with the emission wavelength located well at the slope of the reflection spectrum of the CDF-FBG is used to detect the airflow velocity through the measured reflected optical power from the CDF-FBG. Airflow velocity measurement is achieved with sensitivity of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{321.46}\ \boldsymbol{\mu} \mathbf{W}/(\mathbf{m}/\mathbf{s})$</tex> and the measurement range of 0-0.2 m/s.

articleTitle: Design of Machine Vision Crystal Detection System
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In order to reduce the influence of human eye observation error in flat crystal detection, the plane equal thickness interferometer was upgraded, and the machine vision detection system was established. Building the system requires selecting the camera and designing the matching fixture. The plain crystal detection algorithm was designed and combined with the plain crystal verification procedure. The final experimental results show that the accuracy of measuring flatness of machine vision flat detection system is less than 1 / 5 of the maximum tolerance, and the repeatability is better than 0.01μm. Meet the needs of flat crystal detection.

articleTitle: A Greenhouse Gas Emissions-Aware RSA Scheme Combined with Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient in Optical Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Energy saving and emission reduction have become important topics of concern in various industries. The reduction of greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions in elastic optical networks (EONs) is of great importance. This paper proposes a greenhouse gas emissions-aware RSA scheme combined with deep deterministic policy gradient in EONs. The results show that the proposed scheme reduces the GHG emissions and blocking rate.

articleTitle: Phase Noise Measurment of Mode-Locked Lasers Without Dispersion Management
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We propose a method for precise measurement of repetition-rate phase noise of mode-locked lasers based on dualwavelength delayed self-heterodyne technology assisted by MZI-based repetition-rate multiplier and optical injection locking. Dispersion management is not required.

articleTitle: OSNR Equalization for Extended Bands Based on Online-Trained Model
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Utilizing online training for ML models, we demonstrate channel equalization over 160km L-band link with 3-span amplification, approaching the target OSNR with 10 sets of initial data and 25 rounds of iterative training.

articleTitle: Reflective Curvature Sensor Based on Hole-Assisted Three-Core Fiber
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We demonstrate a reflection curvature sensor based on a hole-assisted three-core fiber (HATCF). HATCF end face is covered with gold film selectively micromachined by femtosecond laser. In the reflectance spectrum of the proposed sensor, two resonance peaks can be observed. The bending direction and curvature are identified by monitoring the wavelength of the two resonance peaks. The maximum curvature sensitivity of the sensor is -14.306 nm/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>.

articleTitle: Positioning Approach in Fiber Vibration Sensing System Based on Time-Frequency Features
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A positioning approach utilizing the dual Mach-Zehnder interferometer-based fiber vibration sensing system was proposed, involving the extraction of time-frequency features from the sensing signal. And a mean positioning error less than ±10 m is achieved.

articleTitle: Simultaneous generation of optical frequency comb and microwave frequency comb utilizing a directly modulated laser
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A simple, power-efficient, and easily adjustable scheme for OFC and MFC generation by utilizing the nonlinear modulation characteristics of DML is proposed and experimentally demonstrated. When the repetition frequency and power of RF signal are set to 6.3 GHz and 2.1 dBm, respectively, a 28-line OFC with flatness of 2.71 dB is generated. By properly controlling the repetition frequency and the power of the RF signal, the comb spacing of OFC can be tuned from 6.7 GHz to 12 GHz. Using a RF signal of 400 MHz with 11-dBm power, a 62-line MFC with flatness range of ±8 dB is obtained. Similarly, the comb spacing of generated MFC can be adjusted from 400 MHz to 3 GHz. This system exhibits the advantages of low cost and easy operation, and provides a new way for simultaneous generation of OFC and MFC.

articleTitle: A Detection Method for Quantum Key Distribution Networks Against DoS Attacks
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: For quantum key distribution networks (QKDNs), we propose a method for detecting DoS attacks and analyzes its detection effectiveness. Simulation results indicate that our detection method performs well in terms of the detection success rate.

articleTitle: Broadband Chaotic Microcomb Parallel High-Speed Random Bit Generation Based on Phase Modulation and Dispersive Component
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A wideband chaotic microcomb generation scheme based on phase modulation and dispersive components is proposed to generate high-speed parallel random bits. Over 150 comb teeth are generated and the rate of one channel reaches 100Gbits/s.

articleTitle: BP Neural Network Assisted Optical Fiber Sensor for High-Precision Demodulation of Salinity and Temperature
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: This article proposes an optical fiber sensor based on fiber surface plasmon resonance (SPR) and Mach-Zehnder interferometer(MZI), which can measure salinity and temperature at the same time. The sensor adopts a transmission structure, which is made of thin-core optical fiber and single-mode optical fiber at both ends. A gold film is used as the metal film to excite SPR, and the MZI effect is generated through the dislocation structure. Experiments have shown that this structure can achieve simultaneous sensing of salinity and temperature. In the temperature range of 32-45°C and the salinity range of 0-20‰, the SPR salinity sensitivity is 3.25nm/‰, the SPR temperature sensitivity is -0.75nm/°C, the MZI temperature sensitivity is -0.39nm/°C, MZI salinity sensitivity is 2.386nm/‰. Machine learning algorithms are used for parameter demodulation to improve the accuracy of dual parameter measurements of salinity and temperature. The sensor has outstanding features such as small size, excellent performance, simple production and high precision.

articleTitle: High-Speed Wideband Wavelength-Swept DFB Laser Array Based on REC Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A wideband fast-sweeping tunable laser array has been designed and fabricated based on reconstruction-equivalent-chirp (REC) technique. The total continuous wavelength tuning range of the multiwavelength laser array is greater than 48 nm with a sweep speed of 5 kHz. By continuous measuring of a fiber Bragg grating (FBG) utilizing the wavelength-swept DFB laser array, it shows a maximum wavelength deviation of less than 2 pm, demonstrating a good wavelength sweeping repeatability.

articleTitle: NBench: A Comprehensive SDN Controller Benchmarking Suite
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Performance evaluation tools are very essential for assessing the capabilities of Software-Defined Networking (SDN) controllers. These tools play a critical role in understanding and quantifying the performance characteristics of SDN controllers. While several open-source performance testing tools, such as CBench, have been developed and are currently in use for evaluating SDN controllers, they have limitations. Specifically, CBench only supports OpenFlow 1.0 and lacks the ability to measure key performance indicators such as topology discovery time, end-to-end link setup time, etc. Moreover, it falls short in terms of system resource utilization and the accuracy of simulated workload representation. In this paper, we introduce NBench, a novel performance evaluation tool designed for SDN controllers. Compared to the well-known CBench, NBench demonstrates significant improvements in system resource utilization and workload simulation accuracy. Additionally, NBench offers a finer granularity of logging and supports the latest versions of the OpenFlow protocol, whereas CBench is limited to version 1.0. Beyond measuring traditional metrics such as Packet-In message response latency and throughput, we have pioneeringly incorporated the measurement of topology discovery time, end-to-end link setup time and link failure recovery time in SDN controllers. To the best of our knowledge, NBench is the first open-source tool to implement these tests.

articleTitle: Subwavelength grating coupler for mid-infrared light coupling to an ultra-thin silicon waveguide
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We demonstrated a key silicon photonic component: a focusing subwavelength grating coupler for mid-infrared light coupling. Specifically, the grating coupler shows an efficiency of -10 dB at a center wavelength of 3.27 μm.

articleTitle: An Ultra-compact Four-channel Wavelength Demultiplexer by Inverse Design
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Integrated photonics devices now play an increasingly significant role in lots of fields. In this paper, we demonstrate a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{1}\times \mathbf{4}$</tex> wavelength demultiplexer (WDM) on standard silicon-on-insulator (SOI) platform working in the O-band by using inverse design algorithm. The device exhibits high transmission efficiencies and low crosstalk characteristics for the four 30nm-spacing channels (1271nm, 1291nm, 1311nm and 1331nm) with the footprint of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{6}\boldsymbol{\mu} \mathbf{m}\times \mathbf{6}\boldsymbol{\mu} \mathbf{m}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{8}\boldsymbol{\mu} \mathbf{m}\times \mathbf{8}\boldsymbol{\mu} \mathbf{m}$</tex>. The average peak transmission efficiencies of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{6}\boldsymbol{\mu} \mathbf{m}\times \mathbf{6}\boldsymbol{\mu} \mathbf{m}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{8}\boldsymbol{\mu} \mathbf{m}\times \mathbf{8}\boldsymbol{\mu} \mathbf{m}$</tex> devices are more than 97.40% and 99.63%. The highest crosstalk is less than -25.38dB and -33.04dB respectively. The lowest bandwidth at a crosstalk of -20dB for the two dimensions are 4.00nm and 8.87nm, which can satisfy the requirement of laser wavelength drift tolerance in current data center transmission systems.

articleTitle: Dimensional Evolutions: Essential Understanding of the Electron-States Architectures
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Starting from 2012, a novel understanding of the continuous dimensional evolutions of the electron-states architectures based on the dimensional similarity functions has been on its long journey of exploration. Now, presented is a well-shaped one.

articleTitle: Joint Optimization of Coding and Shaping for Coherent Optical Communication Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We use differential evolution algorithm to jointly optimize the parameters of forward error correction and probabilistic shaping in coherent optical communication systems. 56-GBaud simulation shows a net data rate gain of 36 Gbit/s.

articleTitle: Adaptive Transceiver Design for High-Capacity Multi-Modal Free-Space Optical Communications
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this invited paper, we review the major challenges that a high-capacity mode-division multiplexed free-space optical communication system could meet, and our recent progress in adaptive transceiver design and implementation to cope with them.

articleTitle: An Integrated Optical Fiber Sensor for Simultaneous Measurement of Temperature and Salinity Based on Sagnac Loop and TFBG
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this letter, we proposed and demonstrated a dual-parameter fiber sensor for simultaneous measurement of temperature and salinity based on Tilted Fiber Bragg Grating (TFBG) and Sagnac loop (SL). Thanks to the extremely high temperature sensitivity of polarization maintaining fiber (PM F) in SL, the designed sensor has a temperature sensitivity of 1.395 nm/°C. Besides, the temperature sensitivity of the core mode in TFBG is 0.009 m/°C and the sensitivity for salinity detection equals to 0.004 nm/% within the wavelength of cladding mode range from 1534 nm to 1535 nm, achieving the measurement of temperature and salinity concurrently. The designed temperature and salinity fiber sensor has certain potential in marine environmental detection.

articleTitle: Multicore Fiber-Tip Nanoforce Probes with Temperature Compensation
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: An ultracompact and highly sensitive multicore fiber-tip nanoforce sensor with temperature compensation is demonstrated. The probes enhance the accuracy and reliability of the sensor while significantly reduce the size of multi-parameter sensor.

articleTitle: Parity-Time Symmetric Optoelectronic Oscillator Based on Four-Wave Mixing Effect in a Semiconductor Optical Amplifier
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Parity-time (PT) symmetric optoelectronic oscillator (OEO) based on the four-wave mixing (FWM) effect in a semiconductor optical amplifier (SOA) is proposed. A single-mode oscillating radio frequency (RF) signal at 9.97 GHz with side mode suppression ratio (SMSR) of 49.47 dB is obtained.

articleTitle: 6-mode SDM transmission over 960 km with a reach extension of 5 times enabled by a 6M-EDFA
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: For the first time, we present 6-mode transmission over 960 km, 5 times longer than before, enabled by an in-line 6-mode Er-doped fiber amplifier. A Gaussian-like Er-doping profile has been proposed to reduce the differential modal gain to 1.15 dB.

articleTitle: LED Strip Quality Detection Based on OpenCV
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: An image processing algorithm for real-time examination of LED light strips is proposed, which enables quick detection of blind LED beads in strips. It is successfully used in production line to replace manual inspections.

articleTitle: Chaotic 2D Cellular Automata Aided DNA Dynamic Encoding Encryption Scheme for Secure CO-OFDM-PON
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A 2D cellular automata aided deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) encoding encryption scheme for OFDM-PON is proposed. The simulation results performed on a CO-OFDM system verify that the scheme greatly enhances the security performance of the system.

articleTitle: Enhancing Data Collection in Wide-Area Internet of Things: A Comprehensive Low-Overhead Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The rapid development of the Internet of Things (IoT) has led to the widespread application of widearea IoT, which offers the advantages of low power consumption and wide coverage. Nevertheless, the scarcity of bandwidth resources poses a significant challenge to the data transmission efficiency of wide-area IoT. Furthermore, the data encoding algorithms currently employed for message payloads tend to exhibit high redundancy and low efficiency. In order to enhance the data transmission efficiency of widearea IoT, our research has yielded the following outcomes: (1) A Template-Based Data Encoding Algorithm (TempEncode) is proposed, which employs data templates to define the message structure. The data template is employed by both senders and receivers, enabling the message payload to be compressed and overhead reduced. (2), a Low Overhead and Enhancing Data Collection (LEAD) approach has been devised for wide-area IoT based on the Message Queuing Telemetry Transport (MQTT) protocol and integrating TempEncode with Robust Header Compression. The experimental results demonstrate that LEAD has reduced the packet size by approximately 50.2% on average in comparison to the original MQTT protocol, thereby achieving efficient data transmission performance.

articleTitle: Micro-Spectrometer with a Beam Splitting Network with Distributed All-Pass Micro-Ring Resonators
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We demonstrate an integrated computational spectrometer with 62 all-pass micro-ring resonators (MRRs), which are distributed in a beam splitting network composed by 31 multi-mode interferometers (MMIs). Measured results show that it has a resolution of 200pm in the C-band. It can be further improved through the optimization of structural parameters and channel number.

articleTitle: Adaptive Microwave Signal Generation Based on the Photonic Real-Time Fourier Transformation Feedback
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Adaptive microwave signal generation based on the photonic Fourier transform feedback is proposed and experimentally demonstrated. Adaptive microwave signals centered at 4, 6, 8 GHz with 2-GHz bandwidth are successfully generated avoiding the interferences.

articleTitle: Large Bandwidth Thin Film Lithium Niobate Electro-Optic Modulator with Periodic Dual-Capacitance Structured Electrodes
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A thin film lithium niobate electro-optic modulator with periodic dual-capacitance structured electrodes has been proposed, achieving a large bandwidth of over 190GHz and a low voltage length product of 1.7 V·cm, with broad application prospects in future communication systems.

articleTitle: High precision frequency source anomaly monitor using Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Timely detection of abnormalities in clock sources is a crucial issue in the miniaturization and widespread adoption of high-performance clock sources. This paper investigates two common types of faults that may occur in chip-scale atomic clocks and assesses the feasibility of using a novel neural network, Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks, for real-time monitoring. Experimental results demonstrate that Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks can effectively monitor clock sources with high accuracy. However, further detailed experiments are necessary to validate the specific features and monitoring durations required for optimal performance.

articleTitle: Secure Key Distribution Based on Dynamic Chaos Synchronization of Semiconductor Laser Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We numerically demonstrate a novel secure key distribution scheme based on dynamic chaos synchronization of semiconductor laser network systems. This scheme circumvents third-party common chaotic injection and achieves a key distribution rate of 0.025 Gbps.

articleTitle: Silicon On-Chip Computational Spectrometer With 32-Channel Meta-Structures
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We report a computational spectrometer on a siliconon-insulator substrate. The device is composed of a beam splitting network and 32 waveguide filter arrays, which consist of numerous meta-structures with unique transmission spectra. The meta-structure and the device have footprints of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.07 \mu\mathrm{m} \times 0.07 \mu\mathrm{m}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1.15 \mu \mathrm{m} \times 24.5 \mu \mathrm{m}$</tex>, respectively. The spectrometer shows a measured resolution of 50 pm around 1550 nm.

articleTitle: Multi-Objective Routing Based on Beluga Whale Optimization in Computing Power Optical Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We propose an improved multi-objective routing method based on Beluga whale optimization in computing power optical networks. Simulation results show that it can decrease delay, improve resource utilization and routing success rate.

articleTitle: Real-Time Human Sleep Conditions Monitoring with Optical Fiber Interferometer Based on a Novel Machine Learning Method
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Optical fiber sensor with fiber interferometer can obtain human vital signs signals more accurately and effectively. A novel machine learning model (PGSVM) is proposed to monitor sleep conditions better with the proposed optical fiber sensor.

articleTitle: Nonlinear FMCW Laser Ranging System Based on Sinusoidal Frequency Modulation
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: This study presents the design of a nonlinear Frequency Modulated Continuous Wave (FMCW) laser ranging system. Contrasting the commonly used triangular wave linear modulation, this study employs sinusoidal wave modulation. The frequency information of the original sinusoidal modulation signal is calculated using the IQ demodulation method. Following the fitting of the measured interference signal at equal frequency intervals, the corresponding distance information is obtained using Fast Fourier Transform (FFT). The principle of this method is thoroughly analyzed and derived, with its correctness subsequently verified through experimental validation.

articleTitle: Design and Performance Analysis of Silica-Based Thermo-Optical Switches Operating in O-Band and C-Band
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Integrated silica-based thermo-optical switches operating in O-band and C-band are designed and experimentally demonstrated. Measurement results show high extinction ratios with low driving voltages for both bands.

articleTitle: Impact of Waist Diameter on Glucose Sensing with MZI-Based Nonadiabatic Tapered MicrolNanofibers
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Glucose sensors are critical in label-free optical biosensing. This study explored the use of nonadiabatic tapered micro/nano optical fibers (NATOFs) with varying diameters (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{10}\ \boldsymbol{\mu}\mathbf{m}, \mathbf{9}\ \boldsymbol{\mu} \mathbf{m}, \mathbf{7}\ \boldsymbol{\mu}\mathbf{m}$</tex>, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{6}\ \boldsymbol{\mu} \mathbf{m}$</tex>) for glucose detection. These fibers were constructed using the Mach-Zehnder interferometry (MZI) principle and the fiber fusion-drawing taper technique. The optical fibers were used to measure refractive indices in glucose solutions with mass fractions ranging from 2 wt% to 20 wt%, where the refractive indices varied between 1.3346 and 1.3608. The findings revealed that decreases in waist diameter substantially enhanced sensor sensitivity, with recorded values of 1851.9 nm/RIU, 2025.8 nm/RIU, 2563.3 nm/RIU, and 2646.4 nm/RIU. Additionally, reducing the diameter of the waist region decreased the free spectral range, enhancing the sensor's accuracy in measuring glucose concentration. This study highlights the potential of micro/nanofiber optic technology in biosensor design, offering new insights for biomedical detection, food quality monitoring, environmental surveillance, and chemical analysis.

articleTitle: Demonstration of Wavelength Selective Attenuator based on Second-order Micro-ring Resonator
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We report the implementation of a two-channel wavelength selective attenuator based on second-order micro-ring resonators (MRRs). The attenuation of each channel is determined by the resonance wavelength deviation between the two cavities in the corresponding MRR, which is controlled by two independent driving voltages. We show continuous attenuation up to 15 dB for different channels with a spacing of 3.9 nm, with the O.5-dB bandwidth being above 125 GHz.

articleTitle: Principal Modes and Anti-Principal Modes of Curved Multimode Fibers
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We demonstrate that multimode fibers possess curved principal modes (CPMs) that resist fiber bending and anti-CPMs that are sensitivity to fiber bending. These modes are expected to be applied in fiber communication and sensing.

articleTitle: Frequency-Domain Optimization of Signal Waveform Shaper in High-Speed Optical Communication Systems Considering ADC Quantization Noise
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: This work presents an approximate differentiable model for fiber channels that is suitable for short-distance optical communication systems with moderate nonlinear effects. The study investigates the impact of quantization and dispersion on the signal by utilizing a differentiable quantization function. A deep complex neural network was constructed using the PyTorch platform, and the optimization of the signal waveform shaper was performed. The optimized waveform shape successfully learned the characteristic features of quantitative noise under dispersion. At the end of the paper, the joint influence of the quantization process and the dispersion process is studied, and the statistical characteristics of the quantization noise are analyzed. The neural network structure proposed in this paper is of great significance for studying the interaction between quantitative effects and dispersion effects.

articleTitle: InP-Based HEMT with Dual δ-Doped Layers Achieving Fmax of 1.43 THz
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We designed a dual δ-doped InP based HEMT with a maximum oscillation frequency of 1.43 THz for THz applications. We simulated and analyzed the device's DC and RF characteristics.

articleTitle: Measurement Method of Laser Linewidth Based on Short-Delayed Self-Heterodyne Michelson Interferometer
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a method for measuring the linewidth of lasers based on a short delay self-heterodyne Michelson interferometer. We enhance the traditional short delay self-heterodyne interference structure by incorporating a Faraday rotating mirror into it, thereby combining the short delay self-heterodyne method with a Michelson interferometer. An advantage of this method is its ability to avoid the influence of 1/f noise and polarization effects. Experimental results demonstrate that this method achieves high computational accuracy.

articleTitle: Failure Prediction Based on Deep Neural Networks in Power Backbone Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A deep neural network based network fault prediction method is proposed. Experimental results show that the proposed method can improve the accuracy compared with several methods.

articleTitle: Structural Soliton Molecules in Spatiotemporal Mode-Locking Yb-Doped Fiber Laser
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Structural soliton molecule (SM) operations were observed in a spatiotemporal mode-locking Yb-doped fiber laser based on nonlinear polarization rotation technique. When the pump power was fixed and the waveplates carefully adjusted, various structural SMs were formed, including <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(2+2)$</tex> type SMs with equal and unequal intensity, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(2+2+2)$</tex> type SM with alternate intensity. Furthermore, numerical simulations give insight into the fine structure of the structural SMs.

articleTitle: Secure Coherent Optical Communication System Based on Dual-Loop Electro-Optic Feedback Phase Encryption
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We propose and demonstrate a novel security-enhanced coherent optical communication system based on dual-loop electro-optic feedback phase encryption, thereby successfully transmitting a 56 Gb/s quadrature phase shift keying (QPSK) signal over a distance of 100 km. Simulation results show that the encryption device effectively suppresses the time delay signature (TDS) and significantly enhances the security of the system.

articleTitle: A Digital Emergency Communication Method for Coal Mining Accident Based on Distributed Acoustic Sensor
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Reliable emergency communication after coal mining accidents can ensure carrying out effective rescue work and reducing casualties. This paper presents a digital emergency communication method for coal mining accident based on distributed acoustic sensor (DAS). The rescue information such as number of trapped workers and injuries, oxygen content, gas consistency, food surplus and water surplus is encoded into digital signals and modulated into vibration signals, which can be generated by intrinsically safe vibrator and monitored by DAS. Experimental results demonstrate that this method can achieve simultaneous multi-point communication utilizing the existing optical cables under coal mine conditions, with a symbol error rate (SER) of less than 1.25%, showing enormous application potential.

articleTitle: Security-Enhanced Chaotic Optical Communication Based on External Electro-Optical Encryption Structure
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We propose a chaotic optical secure communication system based on laser mutual injection and external electro-optical encryption structure. The introduced external electro-optical encryption structure conceals the system time delay signature (TDS) and effectively improves the security of the chaotic optical communication system.

articleTitle: Applications of Dynamic Metasurface Holography in AR/VR
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Metasurfaces are an advanced optical manipulation technology that can control the propagation characteristics of electromagnetic waves through material selection and structural design. Nowadays, metasurfaces have been extensively researched in various optical applications. Among these, metasurfaces have garnered significant attention in augmented reality (AR) and virtual reality (VR) technologies due to their compact structure and precise wave control capabilities. This paper will focus on metasurface holography and its applications in AR and VR, elucidating how metasurface holography can be utilized in this field. Consequently, it will summarize and forecast the development prospects of AR and VR technologies based on metasurface holography.

articleTitle: The influence of medical fiber bending on laser spot distribution of out terminals
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In order to investigate the relationship between the bending radius and spot size and uniformity, and to determine the minimum bending radius of medical fiber. A medical fiber spot acquisition test device was built and the output spots of medical fibers with different core diameters were tested. A thulium 1940 nm laser was used as the laser source and a CCD was used to capture the spot output of the medical fiber at different bend radii. The uniformity of the output spot and the change in the spot size of the medical fiber under different bending radius conditions were recorded and analyzed. The test results show that as the bending radius increases, the spot uniformity becomes better and the spot size becomes larger, and when the bending radius reaches 150 times the diameter of the fiber core, the spot size and uniformity change drastically. It was found that the larger the core diameter, the greater the change in spot after bending. The test results provide a reference basis for the setting of the minimum bending radius of medical fibers.

articleTitle: OOK and ACO-OFDM hybrid system for IM/DD Visible Light Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Thispaper introduces a novel hybrid communication system employing a combination of asymmetric clipped optical orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (ACO-OFDM) and on-off keying (OOK) modulation schemes. The proposed method of signals reconstruction eliminates the need for additional bias current and avoids excess power consumption. At the transmitter, asymmetric signals reconstruction and secondary clipping ensure the transmission signals remains non-negative. Additionally, a layered transmission system is proposed to improve the system's spectrum utilization rate. These hybrid systems enable simultaneous transmission of OFDM and OOK signals, independent recovery of both signals at the receiver, this flexibility supports various quality of service requirements. Simulation results demonstrate successful recovery of both OOK and OFDM signals at the receiver.

articleTitle: A Flexible Pressure Sensor Based on Chirped Fiber Bragg Grating Array for Vital Signs Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A chirped Fabry-Perot interferometric (CFPI) sensor based on two chirped <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{50}-\boldsymbol{\mu} \mathbf{m}$</tex> fiber Bragg gratings is proposed in this paper. The sensing structure packaged with a Polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) can balance wide dynamic range and high sensitivity. Combining miniaturized laser source and photodetector, it can achieve accurate detection of human vital signs conveniently. The promising results of heart pulse measurement in real time allow the sensor to be developed as wearable device for prevention and diagnosis of cardiovascular diseases.

articleTitle: Fiber Mach-Zehnder Interferometer for Simultaneous Measurement of Strain and Temperature Based on Misaligned Peanut-Shape Structure
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: An all-fiber Mach-Zehnder interferometer(MZI) based on modal interference for simultaneous measurement of strain and temperature is proposed and demonstrated. One end of the sensing area is a single mode-multimode-single mode (SMS) splicing structure, and the other is a misaligned peanut-shape structure. This paper explored the influence of different misalignment amounts on the strain sensitivity of sensors. Experimental results have shown that misalignment can improve the strain sensitivity of the sensor, and within a limited range, the strain sensitivity increases with the increase of misalignment amount. The maximum misalignment amount of the sensors fabricated in this paper is 31.8 μm, and its maximum strain sensitivity in the range of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0\sim 800\mu\varepsilon$</tex> is -27.57 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{pm}/\mu\varepsilon$</tex>. It was also used for temperature sensing experiments, and the maximum temperature sensitivity in the range of 30~90 °C is -173.57 pm/°C. By detecting the wavelength shifts of its two different interference dips with temperature and strain, the simultaneous measurement of strain and temperature can be realized.

Author Keywords: Simultaneous measurement of strain and temperature

articleTitle: Ultrathin Silicon Loop Mirror Reflector for 2D PtSe2-On-Waveguide Optical Absorption Enhancement
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We proposed an ultrathin silicon loop mirror reflector for enhancing the PtSe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>-on-waveguide optical absorption. Simulations show that the absorption coefficient of the device is 4.9 times that of a conventional 220 nm-thick silicon strip waveguide.

articleTitle: Co-Generated Brillouin Lasers in a Graphene Over-Modal Microresonator for Multispecies Gas Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Stimulated Brillouin lasers are generated in an over-modal graphene microsphere resonator. By measuring the mode-to-mode laser heterodyne beats, we achieve a label-free chemical gas sensor with tens of part-per-trillion sensitivity for multispecies gas detection.

articleTitle: Experimental Analysis of Correlation Properties in Transition States of Raman Random Fiber Laser
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this work, we experimentally investigate the correlation properties of the RRFL in the transition states for the first time. The temporal correlation increases continuously and finally converges to a stable value, while the shape of the spectral correlation region transitions from a central-correlated square to a sides-correlated cross.

articleTitle: Real-Time Observation of Multimode-Soliton Explosion in a Spatiotemporal Mode-Locked Laser
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Multimode-soliton explosion is experimentally observed in a spatiotemporal mode-locked multimode fiber laser. By using a spatial sampling array, the complex and transient spatiotemporal dynamics of the multimode-soliton explosion are recorded in real time.

articleTitle: Analysis of Influencing Factors in Quantum Neural Network for Solving Classification Problem
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In recent years, the research verification and application exploration of quantum algorithms have developed more rapidly. Quantum algorithm exploration and verification based on quantum computing cloud platform has become one of the important ways. Quantum Neural Network (QNN) combines quantum computing theory with artificial neural network, which is expected to provide potential solutions for classification problems and so on. In the algorithm execution process, factors such as encoding layer, ansatz, and optimizer have all influenced the results. Based on the quantum simulator provided on the quantum computing cloud platform, QNN has been used for experimental validation to study the effects of encoding methods, ansatz types and optimizer variations on the accuracy of QNN training results. Additionally, this artical provides insights into the future trends of quantum algorithm development.

articleTitle: Arbitrary Guide Mode Multiplexer Based on Heterogeneous Integrated Directional Couplers Formed by Multi-Step Photolithography
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We demonstrate a mode multiplexer based on heterogeneous integrated directional couplers formed by multi-step photolithography, which serves to manipulate arbitrary modes (the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{E}_{11}, \mathrm{E}_{21}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{E}_{12}$</tex> modes) from the few-mode waveguide.

articleTitle: Fast Algorithm in Distributed Curvature Sensing Based on OFDR and Helical Weak Gratings Fiber Bundle
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Optical fiber shape sensing technology has attracted widespread attention in fields such as aerospace landing equipment, precision interventional diagnosis, and soft robots. Curvature, being a pivotal parameter in shape sensing technology, demands precise and real-time measurement. In this study, distributed curvature sensing based on helical weak gratings fiber bundle and optical frequency domain reflectometry (OFDR) is proposed. The influence of the weak gratings fiber bundle and cross-correlation algorithm in the demodulation are demonstrated.

articleTitle: Research on Vibration Event Classification in $\Phi-$ OTDR Systems Using MFCC Feature Extraction and Improved Swin Transformer
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, an event recognition method based on MFCC and improved Swin Transformer is proposed for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Phi-$</tex> OTDR event classification of ground-buried sensing fibers. For the scenario of buried optical fibers, MFCC signals and time-domain signals of six types of data samples were selected for comparison. Compared to time domain signals, the average accuracy of MFCC signals on the improved Swin Transformer is 11.95% higher. The feedforward control idea is applied to the structural improvement and information processing process of Swin Transformer. The results of 6 events classification based on 5636 samples show that compared with Swin Transformer, the improved method achieves higher classification accuracy on the self-made dataset, and the average accuracy is increased from 91.499% to 92.674<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> compared with traditional Swin Transformer.

articleTitle: Impact of Analogue-to-Digital Converters on Multi-Channel Digital Nonlinearity Compensation in $200\ \text{Gbits}/\mathrm{s}/\lambda$ Polarization-Multiplexed QAM Transmission Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, the impact of analog-to-digital converter parameters, i.e. resolution bits and sampling rates, on the performance of multi-channel digital nonlinearity compensation has been investigated in high-capacity long-haul optical fiber communication systems.

articleTitle: Terabit Single-Ended Coherent Receiver Using a Partial 3×3 Coupler
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We propose a hardware-efficient single-ended coherent receiver structure using two arbitrary output tributaries of a 3×3 coupler. We experimentally demonstrate 1.008-Tb/s line rate (820-Gb/s net rate) PS-64-QAM signal reception after 80-km standard single-mode fiber transmission.

articleTitle: Superposed 3D-256CAP Constellation Design Based on Geometrically Shaped 3D-16QAM
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Geometric shaping (GS) can significantly enhance the performance of the transmission system. In this paper, a novel 16-ary three-dimensional (3D) constellation structure with a high constellation figure of merit (CFM) is designed by GS. Moreover, a scheme of 3D-GS-256CAP superposed constellation is proposed. Firstly, a 3D-16QAM is superposed with two identical 2D-4QAM to form 3D-256QAM, and then three orthogonal shaping filters are utilized in order to filter the mapping symbols to generate a 3D-GS-256CAP. The results of the simulation indicate that the proposed 16-ary 3D constellation and the superposed 3D-GS-256CAP have superior performance in bit error rate (BER) when compared to other traditional constellations.

articleTitle: Mushroom-mesa Modified Uni-traveling Carrier Photodiodes
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A novel mushroom-mesa modified uni-traveling carrier photodiode is proposed, achieving high-speed, high-RF output power, and low capacitance performance. Its 3dB bandwidth reaches 143 GHz. The proposed structure can be applied for terahertz wave generation.

articleTitle: Nonlinear Impairment Mitigation Based on Full-Link Physically Interpretable E2E Optimization Framework for Over 300-Gbps IM/DD Transmission
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We propose a full-link physically interpretable E2E optimization framework and deploy it in IM/DD fiber optic transmission system. The effectiveness of overcoming nonlinear impairments has been verified, achieving 308.25 Gbps after 0.5-km SMF for CAP-64QAM signals.
