articleTitle: A Resource Orchestration Scheme for Data Synchronization of Distributed Machine Learning in Optical Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We propose a resource orchestration scheme based on heterogeneous network applied to data synchronization in optical network nodes. The simulation results show that this scheme can reduce the total communication delay.

articleTitle: End-to-End Learning of Noise Shaping for OAM Mode Division Multiplexing Transmission
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, an end-to-end noise shaping (E2E-NS) strategy based on autoencoder (AE) is proposed for orbital angular momentum (OAM) mode division multiplexing (MDM) optical fiber communication system. The experimental results show that the bit-error rate (BER) performance of 200 Gb/s carrierless amplitude phase modulation-32 (CAP32) signal with E2E-NS technique outperforms the corresponding signal with traditional NS technique.

articleTitle: A Brillouin Amplified Recirculating Frequency Shifter Loop for Generating High Signal-to-Noise Ratio Optical Frequency Comb
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We demonstrate a scheme for generating high signal-to-noise ratio optical frequency combs based on a Brillouin amplified recirculating frequency shifter loop. The SNR of the comb teeth is improved from 12 dB to 30 dB.

articleTitle: Fast RSOP Tracking in Optical Domain by a Polarization Demultiplexing Device in Coherent Optical Communication Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: By constructing a reset-free polarization controller controlled by an optimized tracking algorithm in FPGA, we demonstrate up to 50 krad/s RSOP tracking in optical domain for coherent optical communication systems without MIMO algorithm.

articleTitle: A Lightweight and Anti-Interference Method for Intrusion Events Recognition with Fiber Optic DAS System
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A lightweight and anti-interference method for intrusion events recognition with fiber optic DAS system is proposed. When faced with high-interference environment, the proposed model achieves the average accuracy of 98.2 % for seven intrusion events with the model size of 1.77 M Flops.

articleTitle: Fiber Optical Borehole Seismometer and its Application in Earthquake Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: This paper reports the recent progresses of fiber optic borehole seismometer and its applications in earthquake monitoring. The earthquake events, solid tides, and temperature change are recorded by the borehole seismometer.

articleTitle: Bulk-Structured Ti2AlC for Mode-Locked Pulses Generation in an All-Normal Dispersion Fiber Laser
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A nanosecond mode-locked Yb-doped fiber laser (YDFL) based on MAX phase Ti<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>AlC saturable absorber (SA) was constructed. This work demonstrates that Ti<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>AlC can serve as a novel modelocker in YDFLs.

articleTitle: Assessment of the Definition Variation Rule for Three-Dimensional Light Field Displays
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: By using the voxel model and the viewpoint analysis method, the definition variation rule at different depths for 3D LFDs is obtained and analyzed, and corresponding measurement method to quantify the display definition is proposed.

articleTitle: Design and Investigation of Electrode for Terahertz Band Photodetector
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: To solve the problem of frequency response attenuation of photodetectors in the terahertz band, a new type of terahertz photodetector electrode structure is designed in this paper using joint simulation design method. Based on technologies such as inductance peaking and arc processing, we have achieved flat output of the photodetector in terahertz band. The simulation results show that the maximum insertion loss of the electrode within 400GHz does not exceed -4dB. After connecting the electrode designed in this paper, the bandwidth of modified uni-traveling carrier photodetector (MUTC-PD) increased by 51% from 217.6GHz to 328.2GHz.

articleTitle: Key Promising Technologies for Submarine Optical Network
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Aiming at the requirements of submarine optical networks, this paper analyzes the key promising technologies in terms of the space-division multiplexing, filterless architecture, low power consumption, and flexibility. The accordingly trends and challenges are addressed.

articleTitle: Research on Submarine Cable Anchor Damage Monitoring Technology Based on a Hybrid Brillouin and Rayleigh Distributed Sensing System
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Submarine cables are critical infrastructure for global communication and energy transmission. However, they are susceptible to damage from anchors, fishing activities, and natural phenomena. This study developed and validated a hybrid Brillouin and Rayleigh distributed sensing system for monitoring submarine cable anchor damage. By integrating Brillouin Optical Time-Domain Analysis (BOTDA) and phase-sensitive optical time-domain reflectometry (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Phi$</tex>-OTDR) technologies, we achieved high sensitivity and spatial resolution measurements of cable strain and vibration with a measurement length of 40 kilometers, a strain measurement variance accuracy of 0.65 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu\varepsilon$</tex> and spatial resolution of 1m. Experimental results showed that the system could accurately detect and quantify cable strain and vibration responses caused by anchor impacts, hooking, and dragging events. Additionally, the vibration signals enabled tracking of the anchor's movement path. This hybrid monitoring method provides a reliable solution for real-time, precise detection of potential threats to submarine cables, enhancing their protection and reducing operational disruptions and maintenance costs.

articleTitle: Enhanced Device Performance of $\text{FAPbBr}_{3}$-based Inverted Light-Emitting Diodes with Sulfobetaine
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The metal halide perovskites have become the most concerned semiconductor materials due to their excellent optoelectronic properties such as high absorption coefficient, high carrier mobility, long carrier diffusion length and low defect density. However, compared with the rapid improvement of the efficiency of perovskite LED devices, the progress in stability of perovskite LEDs is still lagging behind. Inverted iodide-based perovskite LEDs containing ZnO-based electron transport layer are with high device efficiency and long device lifetime, but the device efficiency and working stability of bromide-based perovskite LED still face great challenges. In this work, a dipole molecular stabilizer (sulfobetaine 10) was introduced into <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{FAPbBr}_{\mathbf{3}}$</tex> perovskites to passivate the surface defects of perovskites, and produce high quality perovskite films. An inverted green perovskite LED with a peak EQE of 10.89% and a half lifetime of 3.6 min at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{3600}\ \mathbf{cd}/\mathbf{m}^{\mathbf{2}}$</tex> (at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{20}\mathbf{mA}/\mathbf{cm}^{\mathbf{2}}$</tex> continuous current density) has been realized.

articleTitle: Intensity-Interrogated Hot-Wire Anemometer Based on Cobalt-Doped Fiber Bragg Grating
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: An intensity-interrogated optical fiber hot-wire anemometer with a cobalt-doped fiber (CDF) based fiber Bragg grating (FBG) is proposed. The CDF-FBG is sandwiched between two single mode fibers and is heated optically by using a 1480 nm laser. Experimental results show sensitivity of -648.23 nW/(m/s) at airflow velocity of 0.1 m/s and a measurement range of 0–8 m/s.

articleTitle: HRV Related to Mental Fatigue Obtained Based on MZI-BCG Cushion
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We used a fiber-optic sensor cushion based on Mach-Zehnder interferometer (MZI) to collect BCG signals under mental fatigue, and analyzed the relationship between HRV and mental fatigue.

articleTitle: Investigation of Brightness, Chromaticity, and Color Gamut by Using Different Wavelengths of Blue Light Excitation on Quantum Dot Color Conversion Layers for the Development of Next-Generation Micro-LED Displays
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: This research focuses on exploring the conversion of brightness in green and red quantum dot color converters (QDCCs) when exposed to blue light panels with different wavelengths: 437 nm, 450 nm, and 460 nm. The results indicate that as the wavelength of the blue light decreases, the efficiency of QD emission conversion improves, resulting in increased brightness of the converted QDs. However, it is crucial to consider the potential risks associated with short-wavelength blue light exposure to biological tissues, particularly the eyes. As a result, there is a growing emphasis on the development of longer- wavelength blue light for future QD-based micro-LED displays.

articleTitle: Intelligent Service-Oriented Graph Representation-Assisted High-Efficiency Fine Grain Grooming for OSU-Based OTN
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: This paper proposes an efficient fine-grained grooming scheme based on graph representation to meet the demands of multi-granularity computing power requests. Simulation results demonstrate a significant reduction in cumulative latency and high resource utilization.

articleTitle: Linearly Polarized Mode Demultiplexing Hybrid Based on Multi-Plane Light Conversion
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In order to address the challenges of complex optical front ends of coherent receivers in mode division multiplexing (MDM) fiber communication systems, we propose a linearly polarized (LP) mode de-multiplexing hybrid (MDH) to implement the coherent detection of multiple MDM channels simultaneously based on the multi-plane light conversion technology. This MDH realizes the functions of mode demultiplexing and optical 90-deg mixing with combination of multiple input LP mode signals and the required local oscillator signal, using seven phase plates. After the theoretical modeling and parameter optimization, the proposed MDH can achieved significant performance improvements with insertion loss (IL) of only 1.62dB, mode dependent loss (MDL) of 0.34dB, and crosstalk of -17.42dB. The results show that the proposed MDH has the advantage of greatly simplifying the complex coherent optical front end of large-capacity MDM coherent fiber communication systems.

articleTitle: High Refractive Index Localized Surface Plasmon Resonance Sensor Based on Hollow Core Fiber Filled with Gold Nanowires
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A localized surface plasmon resonance sensor based on hollow-core fibers for high RI detection is proposed, which has good sensing performance and obtains a high sensitivity of 47623.83 nm/RIU in the RI range of 1.430-1.510.

articleTitle: Orbital Angular Momentum Erbium Doped Fiber Amplifier Based on Hybrid Cladding Ring-Core Fiber
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We design an high quality Erbium-doped fiber amplifier based on hybrid cladding ring-core fiber which supports 26 orbital angular momentum (OAM) modes, with differential modal gain (DMG) of less than 0.15dB.

articleTitle: Routing, Modulation Level and Spectrum Assignment Considering Energy Consumption in C+L-Bands Optical Network
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We establish network energy consumption model, propose routing, modulation level, spectrum assignment algorithm considering energy consumption based on DDPG. Simulation results show that this algorithm can effectively reduce energy consumption, decrease blocking rate of requests.

articleTitle: Three-Dimensional Vectorial Magnetic Field Sensor Based on Magnetostrictive Materials
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Terfenol-D is a novel rare-earth material with magnetostrictive properties, and it has been widely used in the field of magnetic field sensing. In this study, we utilized 3D printing technology to construct a three-dimensional sensor framework and combined it with Fiber Bragg Gratings (FBG) to achieve high sensitivity and a wide measurement range for three-dimensional vector magnetic field sensing.

articleTitle: Fabrication of High-Speed Photodiode with Monolithic Integrated InP Microlens
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Back-illumination high-speed photodiode (PD) with monolithic integrated InP microlens was designed and fabricated. The layer structure thickness and doping concentration of the PD were optimized based on carrier transport. Taking into account the effective photosensitive area of the PD and the deviation compensation characteristics of the incident light, an InP microlens was monolithically integrated on the backside of the device. The prepared InP microlens have a diameter of 100 μm, a dome height of 18 μm, and a focal length of 114 μm, with the light spot at the focal point being tested. At a wavelength of 1310 nm, the actual measured bandwidth of the high-speed PD with monolithic integrated InP microlens reached 43 GHz, with a mesa diameter of 18 μm. Furthermore, deviation incident compensation characteristics of the integrated chip were tested and analyzed under horizontal, vertical, and different angle deviations.

articleTitle: Vacuum Quenching Optimization On The Perovskite Films Blade-Coated in Air for Perovskite Solar Cells
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: By optimizing the preparation process of printed perovskite thin films using vacuum quenching assisted crystallization, we effectively separate the rapid nucleation and crystal growth in perovskite polycrystalline thin films. This allows precise control of perovskite crystallization kinetics, leading to the successful preparation of large-area and high-quality perovskite films and devices. Under the optimal conditions, an power conversion efficiency of 17.48% was achieved in small-area cells (0.15 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>), and 15.13% for larger area modules (10.14 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>).

articleTitle: A Few-Shot Learning Equalizer Applied to Optical Communication System
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We propose a fully connected neural network equalizer based on few-shot learning in coherent optical fiber communication systems. The results show that the equalizer we constructed can achieve significant equalization effect with fewer eigenvalues.

articleTitle: Online Learning Raman Scattering Coefficient for C+L Band Transmission Based on WOA Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We propose a method of online learning Raman scattering coefficient for C+L band transmission. The results show that Raman scattering coefficient obtained by the proposed method is more accurate than triangle estimation.

articleTitle: Chaotic Feature Masking Against Attacks on Emitter Identification
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A security approach is proposed to mask the specific emitter identification (ID) attacks by generating 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">320</sup> chaotic ID features. The success rate of forgery attacks is <11%, and the recognition accuracy >90% at 20 dB is verified for the authorized devices.

articleTitle: Pre-Calculated Space-Ground Multi-Dimensional Structure (P-SGMDS): Disaster-Resilient Survivability Design in Terrestrial-Satellite Optical Networks (TSON)
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The disaster-resilient survivability is an important research focus for the terrestrial optical network (TON). The terrestrial-satellite optical network (TSON) brings a new solution to address it. In this article, a pre-calculated space-ground multi-dimensional structure (P-SGMDS) is designed. It can resist random concurrent dual-link failures or any number of fiber link failures. Simulations are conducted in the satellite constellations of Iridium and Starlink phase I. Numerical results show the P-SGMDS has high protection success rate.

articleTitle: MEO-Supervised Traffic Grooming Routing Method for Regional Congestion in LEO Satellite Optical Network
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We propose a MEO-LEO cooperation routing method (MLCR) for regional congestion in the LEO satellite optical network. Simulation results show that MLCR can result in less number of routing calculations, end-to-end transmission delay, and packet drop rate.

articleTitle: Modulation Format Recognition Based on Statistical and Amplitude Features
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A modulation format recognition scheme based on statistical and amplitude features is proposed. Simulation results show that the scheme effectively improves the identification performance of modulation formats in high-speed optical fiber communication.

articleTitle: Experimental Demonstration of Hitless OCS-based DCN Reconfiguration to Steer Multi-Class Traffic: (Invited Paper)
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: To realize hitless optical datacenter network (ODCN) reconfiguration for improving the specific QoS of multiclass traffic flows, we propose a novel topology engineering (TPE) and traffic engineering (TE) scheme, and demonstrate its effectiveness experimentally in a real ODCN testbed.

articleTitle: Weighted Blind Phase Search Algorithm for a PS-QAM Coherent Optical Communication System
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Weighted BPS is proposed for carrier phase recovery of a PS-16QAM coherent optical communication system. The simulation results indicate that compared with traditional BPS, W-BPS obtains a 0.13dB SNR enhancement.

articleTitle: Non-Invasive Cardiac Poincare Analysis Based on Fiber Interferometer
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, a fiber Mach-Zehnder interferometer-based non-invasive cardiac Poincare analysis system is established and discussed, which shows it has great potential in future cardiovascular disease diagnosis.

articleTitle: Simultaneous Measurement of Temperature and Strain Based on Few Modes Tilted Fiber Bragg Grating
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Simultaneous measurement of temperature and strain based on few modes tilted fiber Bragg grating is proposed and demonstrated. Simulation analysis shows that the temperature and strain sensitivities of the LP<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</inf> and LP<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">02</inf> mode center wavelengths of the few modes tilted fiber Bragg grating are different. simultaneous measurement of temperature and strain can be achieved with these two modes.

Author Keywords: Few modes tilted fiber Bragg grating

articleTitle: Low Congestion-Based Routing Algorithm in Optical Network-on-chip
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a congestion avoiding routing algorithm for ONoC based on mesh topology. The simulation results verify the reliability of the algorithm by analyzing end to end delay, memory usage and loss.

articleTitle: High Q Factor Fano Resonances on Dielectric Metasurfaces with Si and Nitride Units
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, an all-dielectric metasurface based on asymmetry of permittivity is designed with high quality factor. The periodic cell of this metasurface consists of two rectangular resonant rings. The metasurface is simulated by Finite Difference Time Domain method and the results show that the transmission spectrum has four Fano resonance peaks in the near-infrared band, and two of the resonance modes are based on quasi-BIC modes, whose quality factors are calculated to be 9651 and 110902, respectively. This study opens new possibilities of metasurface design and device performance.

articleTitle: High-Spatial-Resolution and High-Speed Distributed Vibration Sensing Based on $\varphi-\text{OFDR}$
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We report on a high-spatial-resolution and high-speed phase sensitive optical frequency domain reflectometry system for dynamic measurement based on a distributed feedback laser utilizing the feedback iteration algorithm for linear frequency modulation, which greatly simplifies the experimental equipment and reduces the cost. Fiber with embedded weak reflector array spaced at 4cm intervals has been adopted as the sensing fiber, and a single-branch experimental structure is employed. Demonstration in terms of distributed vibration sensing with a 4cm spatial resolution and 4kHz repetition frequency has been verified, showing excellent crosstalk suppression capability and a high SNR of 50dB.

Author Keywords: phase sensitive optical frequency domain reflectometry

articleTitle: Terahertz Beam-steering Leaky-wave Antennas Applied to Photonic Integrated Transmitter Chips
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: This paper presents a periodic grounded coplanar waveguide leaky-wave antenna for beam steering in terahertz communication, aimed at low-loss integration with a microlens-backed photodetector for terahertz beam-steering photonic integrated transmitter chips. In the operating frequency range of 220 GHz ∼ 320 GHz, the designed terahertz leaky-wave antenna maintains the return loss below -10 dB, and the gain is greater than 10 dBi. The antenna exhibits beam scanning capability, with a total scanning angle of 76°.

articleTitle: Key Technologies for the Next Generation Coherent Passive Optical Network
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: This paper provides analyzed and summarized the key technologies in terms of the next generation downstream simplified coherent passive optical network (PON), upstream burst coherent PON, and the flexible data rate PONs.

articleTitle: A Machine Learning Approach for Laboratory Safety Monitoring under Extreme Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Safety monitoring in laboratories is significant, especially under extreme conditions. In this regard, we proposed a safety monitoring scheme based on machine learning methods. This scheme involves image reconstruction and classification, achieving satisfactory results.

articleTitle: Refractive Index SPR Sensor Based on Side-Polished Capillary Fiber and PDMS
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel surface plasmon resonance (SPR) sensor based on side-polished capillary fiber and polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS), which achieves an ultra-high sensitivity of 4768 nm/RIU in the refractive index detection range of 1. 333–1. 373.

articleTitle: Multimode Fiber Imaging Based on Hydrogel Fiber
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We demonstrate multimode fiber imaging based on hydrogel fibers, which are suitable for biomedical applications due to their biocompatibility and environmental friendliness. High-resolution handwritten images are successfully recovered by utilizing a Pix2Pix image generation network.

articleTitle: Ultrahigh-Repetition-Rate Pulse in a Dissipative Fiber Ring Cavity by Ultrafast Ignition
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel mechanism for ultrahigh repetition rate pulse (UHRP) formation by ultrafast ignition, termed the ultrafast pulse-stimulated four-wave mixing effect in a dissipative ring fiber laser. By employing an ultrafast seeded pulse to initiate a pulse field within a dispersion-managed fiber ring cavity, we stimulate the fourwave mixing effect using a comb filter within the cavity. Through numerical simulations, we achieved UHRPs with a repetition frequency of 275 GHz. The transition from ultrafast pulse to UHRP was monitored in real-time through simulations. Experimental results confirmed the formation of UHRPs via ultrafast ignition of four-wave mixing in a dissipative ring fiber cavity, with the output power reaching up to half a watt.

articleTitle: ZIF-8 Thin Films Synthesized via Chemical Vapor Deposition Technique and its Application for gas Sensing
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: This paper presents the synthesis of metal-organic framework (MOF) films, particularly ZIF-8 films, by the chemical vapor deposition (CVD) technique. It also discusses the gas-sensitive properties of ZIF-8 films and their potential applications in gas sensors.

articleTitle: High-Resolution Spectroscopy Based on Interleaved Brillouin Optical Frequency Comb
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We propose a high-resolution spectroscopy system based on an interleaved Brillouin optical frequency comb. The high spectral resolution is verified by measuring FBG transmission over a bandwidth of 5.4nm.

articleTitle: Inverse Design of Continuous Domain Bound State All-Dielectric Metasurface Based on Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A deep learning-based reverse design method for metasurface structures is proposed, which can quickly and effectively deal with the relationship between continuous parameter structure and electromagnetic response, and realize the accurate prediction of structure parameters.

articleTitle: Laser Performance of DBR Fiber Lasers Packaged
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We constructed a distributed Bragg reflector (DBR) single-frequency fiber laser (SFFL). The laser performance of the unpackaged and packaged lasers is tested separately. After packaging, the performance of the laser has been greatly improved.

articleTitle: Lightweight DenseNet for Submarine Cable Anchor Damage Event Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Rapid identification and localization of submarine cable anchor damage events is crucial and challenging for its safe and stable operation. In this paper, a submarine cable anchor damage recognition system using lightweight DenseNet network is developed by pruning the four fully connected layers in the original code into two layer and adjusting the parameters of the convolutional layer to make it lightweight. Experiments show that the accuracy reaches from 93.06% to 97.03%, the model size is reduced from the original 44.8m to 4.48m, and the total training time of the model is reduced from 4698s to 3296s. The lightweight DenseNet network proposed in this paper reduces the cost of time and reduces the size of the model without affecting the recognition accuracy.

articleTitle: An Enhanced Encoding Method for Photonic Spiking Neural Network Based on the VCSEL-SA
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The concept of neuromorphic computation, implemented by physical devices, has obtained significant attention owing to its exceptional performance in handling specific tasks. These devices have the characteristics of neuron-like output and can mimic the brain's methodology of information transmission and computation. However, a significant limitation lies in the prevalent encoding methods for neuromorphic computation, which primarily rely on either rate or temporal encoding, thereby causing inefficiencies in the execution of computational tasks. In this article, we introduce an effective and biologically inspired encoding approach for a photonic spiking neural network (PSNN), utilizing vertical-cavity surface-emitting lasers with an embedded saturable absorber (VCSELs-SA). Our method encodes data information by modulating the intensity of an injection rectangular pulse, which subsequently triggers the emission of spikes from the VCSELs-SA. The proposed PSNN can recognize four spiking patterns and classify the Iris dataset. What's more, we get an accuracy of 94.67% in the classification task with only six neurons.

articleTitle: Cost-Efficiency and Low Latency Oriented Reliable Deployment For TDM-PON Based 5G RAN in Power Distribution Network
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: This article discusses cost-efficient and low latency oriented reliable deployment for TDM-PON based 5G RAN in power distribution network. A multi head attention enhanced DQN algorithm is proposed for distribution network protection services.

articleTitle: GN-Based Optimization of the Geometric Shaping Constellations for the Non-Linear Fiber Channel
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A geometric shaping optimization scheme based on the Gaussian noise (GN) model incorporating self-phase modulation (SPM) correction is proposed. The simulation results show that the proposed GS-64QAM obtains 0.38 dB OSNR gain at the BER of HD-FEC.

articleTitle: Experimental Demonstration of Short-Reach C-Band 44.112 Tbps Coherent Optical Transmission with Sand L-Band Dummy Channels Based on PS-4096-QAM
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We demonstrate a coherent transmission system covering S-, C-, + L-band over 20km standard single mode fiber (SSMF) based on PS-4096-QAM. The C-band throughput is measured to be overall 44.112 Tb/s after transmission.

articleTitle: A Phase Modulation Based and Frequency Stabilized Optoelectronic Oscillator Using a Self-Phase Locking Loop
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A phase modulation based and frequency stabilized optoelectronic oscillator (OEO) by use of a self-phase locking loop (SPLL) is demonstrated. This SPLL is utilized to control the shifted phase of a tunable phase shifter in the oscillating loop. In this way, the frequency stability of this OEO can be improved without the need of an external RF source. The experimental results for a 10-GHz OEO show that the frequency fluctuations are decreased to less than 7 kHz within an hour, and the Allan deviation is reduced by 2 orders of magnitude.

articleTitle: A High-Performance Circular Polarizer
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A high-performance circular polarizer is demonstrated. Its ellipticity, degree of polarization and insertion loss are 44.44°, 98.45% and 1.12 dB. The isolation is more than 30 dB in the range of 1310 ± 30 nm.

articleTitle: Dynamic Refractive Index Sensing of Water-Ice Phase Transition with a Single Fiber Grating
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We show that a single titled fiber Bragg grating (TFBG) can perform in-situ monitoring of refractive index changes during a water-ice phase transition process. The resonant wavelengths of TFBG modes are sensitive to temperature, strain, and surrounding refractive index (SRI) variations, induced by the phase transition. Based on the differential wavelength shifts of different TFBG resonances, the temperature and strain effects can be calibrated and eliminated. Thus, the remaining wavelength shifts induced by SRI can be obtained for monitoring the water-ice phase transition.

articleTitle: Multi-dimensional Resource Measurement Based on Entropy Weight Method in Computing Power Optical Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We propose a multi-dimensional resource measurement approach based on the entropy weight method, which dynamically determines index weights and calculates scores of nodes. Simulation results show that it can effectively select nodes with high adaptability.

articleTitle: Coherently Controlled Absorption of Few-Layered Electromagnetic Metamaterials
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A kind of few-layered electromagnetic metamaterial has been designed to generate coherent perfect absorption phenomena in the terahertz band and the absorption can vary in the range of 0–1 according to the phase difference.

articleTitle: Pricing Strategy for Computing Tasks in Computing Power Networks: A Non-Cooperative Sequential Game Strategy
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We propose a game theory-based dynamic pricing strategy for computing tasks in CPN. Simulation results show the strategy improves network revenue by 12% and achieves the balance of computing resource provisioning among different data centers.

articleTitle: Sensing Bandwidth Enlargement with Orthogonal Codes and Mismatched Filters in Distributed Acoustic Sensing System
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: With orthogonal codes and corresponding mismatched filters, the multiplexing of sensing channels on the same spectrum is first achieved in distributed acoustic sensing (DAS) based on Rayleigh backscattering, doubling the sensing bandwidth.

articleTitle: Demonstration of 4-Mode Cladding-pumped EDFA Based on Tapered Fiber
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A 4-mode EDFA was constructed to compare the two cladding pumping schemes, and the results show that helix side pumping is more conducive to increased gain and reduced DMG.

articleTitle: Genetic Algorithm Assisted Power Allocation in TFDMA Coherent Point-to-Multipoint Passive Optical Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We propose and demonstrate a power allocation scheme assisted by the genetic algorithm in TFDMA coherent passive optical networks. The performance of flexible rate ONUs can be significantly improved for diverse link conditions.

articleTitle: Compact Vector Bending Sensor Based on Hole-Assisted Optical Fiber
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A highly sensitive, compact and robust vector bending sensor based on in-fiber directional coupler is proposed and experimentally demonstrated. The sensor is constructed by directly sandwich-splicing a segment of single eccentric hole-assisted dual-core fiber between two single mode fibers (SMFs). The bending responses of the sensor are experimentally measured in the curvature range of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{0-4.8248}\mathbf{m}^{-\mathbf{1}}$</tex>. The bending sensitivities are <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-\mathbf{13.83}\ \mathbf{nm}/\mathbf{m}^{-\mathbf{1}}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{15.48}\ \mathbf{nm}/\mathbf{m}^{-\mathbf{1}}$</tex> at 0° and 180° bending direction. Furthermore, a two-dimensional vector bending sensor based on hole-assisted three-core fiber coupler is demonstrated. Two completely discrete resonance dips are observed in the transmission spectrum. The bending response of the proposed sensor is investigated at 360° range with a step of 45°. The bending curvature and direction can be identified by interrogating the wavelengths of the two resonance dips, and the maximum curvature sensitivity of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-\mathbf{50.62}\ \mathbf{nm}/\mathbf{m}^{-\mathbf{1}}$</tex> is achieved at 0° direction.

articleTitle: High-Order-Mode Multi-Wavelength Random Fiber Laser Based on Brillouin and Rayleigh Scattering in Few Mode Fibers
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We demonstrated a multi-wavelength random fiber laser with high-order spatial mode emission by utilizing stimulated Brillouin scattering gain and distributed Rayleigh scattering in few-mode fibers.

articleTitle: A Magnetic Field Fiber Sensor Based on Side Hole Fiber Filled with Magnetic Fluid in Fiber Ring Laser Cavity
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We proposed a simple magnetic field fiber sensor based on magnetic fluid (MF) filled side hole fiber (SHF) in fiber ring laser (FRL) system. The output wavelength of the laser shifts with the change of magnetic field, and its sensitivity is 0.4365 nm/mT at the range of 2 mT- 10 mT. Thanks to the high signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and narrow linewidth of the laser cavity, its SNR is as high as 50 dB, and the 3-dB linewidth is 0.1 nm, without losing sensitivity. The designed sensor is expected to have potential applications in navigation system.

articleTitle: Noise Interference Impact Degree-Aware Routing in Quantum Key Distribution Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We introduce a noise interference impact degree (NIID), which quantifies the extent to which noise interference affects the network layer. The results demonstrate the feasibility of our scheme in significantly reducing the service blocking rate.

articleTitle: Inverse-Design of Random Fiber Laser with Saddle-Shaped Spectrum
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Based on convolutional neural network and dual-energy-level NLSE model, we realize the inverse design of RFL, for the first time. And combined with the dual-cavity coupling structure, a broadband saddle-shaped spectrum is realized experimentally.

articleTitle: High Sensitivity Fiber Fabry Perot NH3 Sensor Based on PMMA Film
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Ammonia <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\text{NH}_{3})$</tex> has been being widely used in medical and industrial applications. In this study, we demonstrated a fiber extrinsic Fabry-Pérot interferometer (EFPI) sensor, the interference cavity of which is configured by the end-face of single-mode fiber (SMF) and the polymethyl methacrylate (PMMA) film in a capillary. Based on high response characteristics of PMMA film for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{NH}_{3}$</tex>, the sensor achieves a sensitivity of up to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$500 pm/ppm$</tex> for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{NH}_{3}$</tex> concentration detection experimentally.

articleTitle: A Precision Fiber Optic Microseismic Monitoring System for Underground Coal Mines
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Microseismic monitoring has been predominantly taken by using moving-coil geophones. However, the drawbacks including small dynamic range, susceptibility to electromagnetic interferences, and non-intrinsically safe, seriously hinder the further progress and applications of monitoring system itself. This paper presents the development of novel precision fiber optic microseismic monitoring system. The overall composition, sensor design and interrogation scheme are introduced in detail. The results show that the system achieves a bandwidth of 1 Hz to 320 Hz, 86.5 dB dynamic range and a minimum detectable acceleration of 0.708 mm/s<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>at 30 Hz. The field test results show that this system has great potential for safety monitoring of underground coal mines.

articleTitle: Joint Optimization of Working and Protection Paths for RSA in Mixed-Grid Optical Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The elastic optical network (EON) is regarded as the next generation optical network with finer spectrum granularity and higher spectrum utilization. However, the migration process from wavelength division multiplexing (WDM) network to EON cannot be completed immediately. Therefore, the fixed-grid nodes and flex-grid nodes will coexist in the mixed-grid optical network, which challenges the routing and spectrum allocation (RSA). In this work, a joint optimization of working and protection paths routing and spectrum allocation (JOWP-RSA) algorithm is proposed to select the allocation strategy with the lowest spectrum occupancy and the highest spectrum availability. The simulation results demonstrate that the JOWP-RSA algorithm can reduce the proportion of protection resources by about 18.2% and reduce the block ratio by about 50%.

articleTitle: Fiber Bragg Grating Sensing System Utilizing Fast and Wideband REC-DFB Laser Array
publicationTitle: 2024 22nd International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A fast and wideband wavelength-swept laser (WSL) utilizing the reconstruction-equivalent-chirp (REC) technique, integrated with 24 DFB lasers, is proposed and experimentally demonstrated. Additionally, a high-speed FBG sensing system using field-programmable gate arrays (FPGAs) is proposed and demonstrated, achieving stable high-speed sweeping with a wavelength coverage of 50.4 nm and a sweeping frequency of up to 5.85 kHz without mode hopping. The FBG sensing system has a solid-state design without moving parts, enabling real-time, high-speed, and stable monitoring of temperature, pressure, strain, and displacement. Furthermore, the system is cost-effective and anticipated to have diverse industrial applications.
